parts.body: It's always a pleasure to see our charming little village, is it not?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Fysiká, kai eínai etsi logo ton terástion prospatheión mas! /

parts.body: I love sunny days!

parts.body: Why don't you?

parts.prefix: v1;150;O ílios kaíei! Misó tin kapsa! /
parts.body: The sun burns! I hate being the outside!

parts.body: You act like a zombie!
parts.job: uk|You act like a zombie!

parts.body: Maybe I am...

parts.prefix: v1;0;Einai panta efxaristo na xazeueis to xorio mas, etsi den einai? /
parts.body: It is always a pleasure to see our nice little village, isn't it?
parts.job: uk|It is always a pleasure to see our nice little village, isn't it?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Fysiká eínai! Éxoume ksodépsei tóso polý chróno douleuontas se aftó to méros. /
parts.body: Of course it is! We've spent so much time working on this place.
parts.job: uk|Of course it is! We've spent so much time working on this place.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Eínai sxedón san tin mitropoli, ópos prin erthoume edó. /

parts.job: uk|It's almost like home, just like before we came here.

parts.prefix: v2;90;Aftó eínai to spíti mas tóra, aplá prépei na to apodextoúme. /

parts.job: uk|This is our home now, we just have to accept that.

parts.prefix: v1;120;Kséro, tha to dextó me ton kairó ... /
parts.body: I know, I'll accept that in time...
parts.job: uk|I know, I'll accept that in time...

parts.prefix: v1;0;Einai panta efxaristo na xazeueis to xorio mas, etsi den einai? /
parts.body: It is always a pleasure to see our nice little village, isn't it?
parts.job: uk|It is always a pleasure to see our nice little village, isn't it?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Fysiká eínai! Éxoume ksodépsei tóso polý chróno douleuontas se aftó to méros. /
parts.body: Of course it is! We've spent so much time working on this place.
parts.job: uk|Of course it is! We've spent so much time working on this place.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Eínai schedón san sto spíti, akrivós ópos prin írthame edó. /
parts.body: It's almost like home, just like before we came here.
parts.job: uk|It's almost like home, just like before we came here.

parts.job: uk|This is our home now, we just have to accept that.

parts.prefix: v1;120;Pragmati einai, aftí i syzítisi me ékane na to syneiditopoiíso. /
parts.body: Indeed it is, this conversation has made me realize that.
parts.job: uk|Indeed it is, this conversation has made me realize that.

rows.raw: //v1;0;To sitári kai ta stafýlia mas afksánontai polý fétos. / Our wheat and grapes have been growing very well this year.
//v2;30;Nai, oi agrótes anaféroun proodo, kai dokimásate kai to krasí? / Yes, the farmers are reporting record harvests and have you tried the wine?
//v1;60;Den éxoume tavérna gia na kánoume krasí ... / Um, we have no tavern to make wine...
//v2;120;A..., tóte ti epina exthes ?!/ Oh..., then what did I drink yesterday?!
//v1;0;To sitári kai ta stafýlia mas afksánontai polý fétos. / Our wheat and grapes have been growing very well this year.
//v2;30;Nai, oi agrótes anaféroun proodo, kai dokimásate kai to krasí? / Yes, the farmers are reporting record harvests and have you tried the wine?
//v1;60;Ego exo! To eksairetikó romaïkó mas krasí éxei kalýteri géfsi apó poté!/ I have! Our fine Roman wine tastes better than ever!
//v2;90;Kséro, den eínai katapliktikó? Eíxa pénte olóklira boukália exthes. To kalýtero krasí pou ipia poté! / I know, isn't it amazing? I had five whole bottles yesterday. Best wine I have ever had!

//v1;120;Pénte olóklira boukália? Amartaneis antrope mou! Akómi kai an eínai mia exairetikí epochí, kindynéveis na gíneis methystakas me toso poly krasi!/ Five whole bottles? You need to slow down man! Even with it being a great season, you risk becoming a drunkard with drinking that much wine!
//v2;150;Tha eímai kalá ótan o ponokéfalos aftós perasei ... / I'll be fine once this headache goes away...
//v1;0;Xreiazómaste mia tavérna gia na ftiáksoume to krasí ./ We need a tavern to make wine up and running soon.

//v2;30;Pos? Giatí? Entaksei, to krasí eínai kaló, allá éna olókliro ktírio, mono gia to krasí? Prépei na váloume proteraiótites sti seira! / What? Why? Sure, wine is good, but a whole building for wine? We need to get your priorities straight!
//v1;60;Dokímasa lígo xymó Norman exthes. Ítan friktó! Pós tous aresoun auta tous agrious? / I tried some Norman cider yesterday. It was horrible! How do those savages like that?
//v2;90;Giatí dokimázeis ta potá ton Barbaron? Eísai ilíthios?! / Why are you trying the savages' drinks? Are you an idiot?!
//v2;130;Pánta na píneis romaïkí ousía! ROMAÏKÍ OUSÍA! / Always drink Roman stuff! ROMAN STUFF!

parts.prefix: v1;0;I sodeia ton sitiron paei kala fetos, opos kai ton stafylion. Euge! /
parts.body: Wheat is growing very well this year, so are grapes as well. Brilliant, no?
parts.job: uk|Wheat is growing very well this year, so are grapes as well. Brilliant, no?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Pragamati, etsi faínetai: Éxoume to períergo kairo edo na efcharistísoume. /
parts.body: Yes, it seems so: We have the weird weather here to thank.
parts.job: uk|Yes, it seems so: We have the weird weather here to thank.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Akoma kai an den bgazei noima! /
parts.body: Even if it doesn't make any sense to me!
parts.job: uk|Even if it doesn't make any sense to me!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Thymáste tin kataigída tis proales? Milao gia ekeinon ton kolokairo! /
parts.body: Do you remember the thunderstorm we had? I mean the really heavy one!
parts.job: uk|Do you remember the thunderstorm we had? I mean the really heavy one!

parts.prefix: v2;30;Fysiká. Sxedon katastráfike olokliri i synkomidí mas. O Theos na mas prostateuei. /
parts.body: Of course. Almost ruined our harvest. Nature is quite impressive, eh?
parts.job: uk|Of course. Almost ruined our harvest. Nature is quite impressive, eh?

parts.prefix: v1;60;Megalo to onoma tou! Paraligo na me xtipisei o satanas me kerauno! /
parts.body: Impressive is one thing. But I was almost hit by a lightning bolt!
parts.job: uk|Impressive is one thing. But I was almost hit by a lightning bolt!

parts.prefix: v2;100;Katse ore sto spiti sou xristiane! Afou ekso itan epikyndina! /
parts.body: You were not in your house? You know it's dangerous outside during a storm!
parts.job: uk|You were not in your house? You know it's dangerous outside during a storm!

parts.body: Live and learn.
parts.job: uk|Live and learn.

parts.body: I am not feeling well...
parts.job: uk|I am not feeling well...

parts.body: What's wrong with you? Are you sick?
parts.job: uk|What's wrong with you? Are you sick?

parts.body: Nope, I j-j-just remembered someth-thing.
parts.job: uk|Nope, I j-j-just remembered someth-thing.

parts.prefix: v2;100;Den akougetai kala. Eísai sígouros oti den eísai árrostos? /
parts.body: You sound really bad. Are you sure you are not sick?
parts.job: uk|You sound really bad. Are you sure you are not sick?

parts.body: N-no, I just f-feel scared.
parts.job: uk|N-no, I just f-feel scared.

parts.body: So what happened?
parts.job: uk|So what happened?

parts.prefix: v1;180;Katá ti diárkeia tis t-teleftaía kataigídas, perpátisa ékso apo to chorio-o, íksera oti den mporoúsa na páo píso sto xorio prin teliosei i kataigída. Etsi krýftika káto apo éna déntro. /
parts.body: During the l-last thunderstorm. I walked outside the v-v-village, I knew I could not get back to the village before the storm. So I hid under a tree.
parts.job: uk|During the l-last thunderstorm. I walked outside the v-v-village, I knew I could not get back to the village before the storm. So I hid under a tree.

parts.prefix: v2;210;Pas kala more? tha mporouses na eixes pethanei! /
parts.body: You risked your life outside the village! You could have died!
parts.job: uk|You risked your life outside the village! You could have died!

parts.prefix: v1;240;Loipon, ímoun asfalís. Sti synécheia,pou les, eída éna gouroúni. Mpam! To xtypise keraunos . Kai ... a-afto sikothike kai kiníthike l-san ki emás, Kai me kinygise me mia spatha! /
parts.body: Well, I was safe. But then I saw a pig. The lighning struck it. And the dead p-pig... I-it got up and moved l-like us, ch-chasing me with a shiny sw-sword!
parts.job: uk|Well, I was safe. But then I saw a pig. The lighning struck it. And the dead p-pig... I-it got up and moved l-like us, ch-chasing me with a shiny sw-sword!

parts.body: You are talking nonsense. It must have been a nightmare.
parts.job: uk|You are talking nonsense. It must have been a nightmare.

parts.body: It was true! True! True! True!
parts.job: uk|It was true! True! True! True!

parts.prefix: v2;350;Trelathikes ore. Pane pies kana potiri, na iremiseis. /
parts.body: You are mad. Go get some wine, and calm down.
parts.job: uk|You are mad. Go get some wine, and calm down.

parts.body: I'll d-do that. May-Maybe it will help.
parts.job: uk|I'll d-do that. May-Maybe it will help.

parts.prefix: v1;0;Ax ... Souvláki, to éna kai monadiko fagito! /
parts.body: Ah... Souvlaki, the one and only food!
parts.job: uk|Ah... Souvlaki, the one and only food!

parts.prefix: v2;30;...I panagia na mas exei kala ... /
parts.body: Holy Maria guard us...
parts.job: uk|Holy Maria guard us...

parts.body: Holy trinity give us strenght!
parts.job: uk|Holy trinity give us strenght!

parts.body: Amin
parts.job: uk|Amin

parts.body: Amin...
parts.job: uk|Amin...

parts.body: Now, where did I put the salt?
parts.job: uk|Now, where did I put the salt?

parts.prefix: v1;0;Variemai. Ola eínai pánta to ídio edo. /
parts.body: Boring. Everything is always the same here.
parts.job: uk|Boring. Everything is always the same here.

parts.prefix: v2;30;Touláxiston i zoi edo eínai eirinikí. /
parts.body: At least it is peaceful.
parts.job: uk|At least it is peaceful.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Típota to idiaítero gia éna apomakrysméno xorio san to diko mas! /
parts.body: Nothing special for a remote village like ours!
parts.job: uk|Nothing special for a remote village like ours!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Otan ímoun mikros, íthela na eínai énas exerevnitís, na anakalýpsoun néa edáfi kai na pliroún endiaférontes néous anthropous. Allá tora? Eímai kollísei se afto to apomakrysméno chorioudáki. Thélo na páo kai na episkeftheíte néa méri. /
parts.body: When I was young, I wanted to be an explorer, discover new lands and meet interesting new people. But now? I am stuck in this remote little village. I want to go and visit new places.
parts.job: uk|When I was young, I wanted to be an explorer, discover new lands and meet interesting new people. But now? I am stuck in this remote little village. I want to go and visit new places.

parts.prefix: v2;30;Allá den tha vreíte megáli diaforá sto állo chorio. Eímaste oloi lígo polý to ídio. /
parts.body: But you won't find much difference in the other village. We're all pretty much the same.
parts.job: uk|But you won't find much difference in the other village. We're all pretty much the same.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Den milo gia ta choriá. Milo gia tis poleis, í akoma kai i Poli! /
parts.body: I am not speaking about villages. I am speaking about towns, or even the city!
parts.job: uk|I am not speaking about villages. I am speaking about towns, or even the city!

parts.body: THE city? You mean Constantinople?
parts.job: uk|THE city? You mean Constantinople?

parts.prefix: v1;120;Nai! To kéntro tis éndoxis aftokratorías mas. Eínai to thávma tou kosmou. /
parts.body: Yeah! The centre of our glorious empire. It is the wonder of the world.
parts.job: uk|Yeah! The centre of our glorious empire. It is the wonder of the world.

parts.prefix: v1;150;Ypárchoun perissoteroi apo 500 000 ánthropoi pou zoun ekeí, boreíte na imangine afto?! /
parts.body: There are more than 500 000 people living there, can you imangine that?!
parts.job: uk|There are more than 500 000 people living there, can you imangine that?!

parts.prefix: v2;180;Akoúgetai adýnato gia ména. 500 000 ánthropoi se éna méros? /
parts.body: Sounds impossible to me. 500 000 people in one place? Dream on!
parts.job: uk|Sounds impossible to me. 500 000 people in one place? Dream on!

parts.body: Don't drink wine alone!
parts.job: uk|Don't drink wine alone!

parts.prefix: v2;30;To na pineis mazí eínai pio diaskedastiko! /
parts.body: Drinking together is more fun!
parts.job: uk|Drinking together is more fun!

parts.body: Cheers for the wine!
parts.job: uk|Cheers for the wine!

parts.body: Cheers!
parts.job: uk|Cheers!

rows.raw: //v1;0;Tha eímai o archigos tou chorioú argotera, oldie! / I'll be the head of the village later, oldie!
//v2;30;Min eísai toso thrasýs, agoráki. Í tha páreis kana chastoúki! / Don't be so cheeky, little boy. Or you will get a slap!
//v1;60;Kai ego to idio! / And I'll get you slapped then!
//v2;105;Traba fyge tora! / Maybe you've learned something!

parts.prefix: v1;0;O pateras mou eínai pio dynatos apo ton diko sas. /
parts.body: My dad is stronger than yours.
parts.job: uk|My dad is stronger than yours.

parts.prefix: v2;30;Ochi! O patir mou eínai o pio dynatos sto chorio! /
parts.body: No! My dad is the strongest in the village!
parts.job: uk|No! My dad is the strongest in the village!

parts.prefix: v1;60;Ochi! O pateras mou eínai o pio dynatos stin Autokratoría! /
parts.body: Not! My dad is the strongest in the empire!
parts.job: uk|Not! My dad is the strongest in the empire!

parts.prefix: v2;90;Nai kala! O patir mou eínai o pio dynatos ston kosmo! /
parts.body: Impossible! My dad is the strongest in the world!
parts.job: uk|Impossible! My dad is the strongest in the world!

parts.prefix: v1;120;Sígoura o pateras mou tha mporoúse na nikísei ton diko sou se ligotero apo dýo chtypímata! /
parts.body: I bet my dad could beat yours in less than two hits!
parts.job: uk|I bet my dad could beat yours in less than two hits!

parts.body: Get your dad prepared for a fight!
parts.job: uk|Get your dad prepared for a fight!

parts.body: Girls are stupid.
parts.job: uk|Girls are stupid.

parts.prefix: v1;0;Échete dei pouthená tin koúkla mou? Den boro na to vro ... /
parts.body: Have you seen my doll anywhere? I can't find it...
parts.job: uk|Have you seen my doll anywhere? I can't find it...

parts.prefix: v2;30;Dose mou píso to spathí mou kai tha tin páreis píso! /
parts.body: Give me my sword back and you will get it back!
parts.job: uk|Give me my sword back and you will get it back!

parts.body: You stole it! Thief!
parts.job: uk|You stole it! Thief!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Écheis dei ta kainoúrgia roúcha mou? /
parts.body: Have you seen my new clothes?
parts.job: uk|Have you seen my new clothes?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Eíste mia pragmatikí desposini agapiti mou. Ta panta sou tairiázoun! /
parts.body: You are a real beauty my dear. Everything fits you!
parts.job: uk|You are a real beauty my dear. Everything fits you!

parts.prefix: v1;60;Allá den eímai toso omorfi oso eseis! /
parts.body: But I am not as beautiful as you!
parts.job: uk|But I am not as beautiful as you!

parts.body: Ohh that's not true, $targetfirstname!
parts.job: uk|Ohh that's not true, $targetfirstname!

parts.body: Have you seen my new clothing?
parts.job: uk|Have you seen my new clothing?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Eiste mia pragmatikí desposini agapiti mou. Ta panta sou tairiázoun, agapité $targetfirstname mou! /
parts.body: You are a beauty. Everything suits you, my dear $targetfirstname!
parts.job: uk|You are a beauty. Everything suits you, my dear $targetfirstname!

parts.prefix: v1;60;Allá den eímai toso omorfi oso eseis! /
parts.body: But I am not as beautiful as you!
parts.job: uk|But I am not as beautiful as you!

parts.body: True.
parts.job: uk|True.

parts.prefix: v1;0;Écheis dei ta kainoúrgia roúcha mou, $targetfirstname? /
parts.body: Have you seen my new clothes, $targetfirstname?
parts.job: uk|Have you seen my new clothes, $targetfirstname?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Nomízo oti paliá roúcha sas fainotan polý kalýtera pano sás. /
parts.body: I think your old clothes looked much better on you.
parts.job: uk|I think your old clothes looked much better on you.

parts.job: uk|They all just shared everything equally. It made trading with them very difficult.

parts.prefix: v2;210;Katakaimene empore. Touláchiston eínai píso sti Romaïkí Aftokratoría, makriá apó aftoús tous bárbarous. /
parts.body: Poor trader. At least he is back in the Roman Empire, away from those barbarians.
parts.job: uk|Poor trader. At least he is back in the Roman Empire, away from those barbarians.

parts.prefix: v1;240;Symfonó! I Romaïkí Aftokratoría eínai i kalýteri gi gia empório! /
parts.body: I agree! The Roman Empire is the best land to trade!
parts.job: uk|I agree! The Roman Empire is the best land to trade!

rows.raw: //v1;0;Geiá sou! Den faínetai na eíste polý efcharistiménoi símera / Hello! You don't seem to be very happy today.
//v2;30;Nai, den ypárchei tavérna gia na pioúme. / Yeah, there is no tavern for us to drink at.
//v1;60;Éfchomai na ypirche mia tavérna. Tóte tha boroúsame na pioúme romaïkó krasí. / Yeah, I wish there was a tavern. Then we could drink Roman wine.
//v1;0;Elpízo óti den tha chreiasteí na vgoúme éxo kai na polemísoume opoiondípote bárbaro ópote sýntoma. / I hope we don't have to go out and fight any barbarians anytime soon.

//v2;30;Ti? Eímaste stratiótes, i douleiá mas eínai na bgoúme éxo kai na skotósoume bárbarous. Giatí tha beíte ston strató an den sas arései na agonízeste? / What? We are soldiers, our job is to go out and kill barbarians. Why would you join the army if you don't like fighting?

//v1;60;Skéftika óti i zoi mou tha ítan efkolóteri, to móno pou perímena na káno eínai na stamatíso kai na skotóso lígous óchlous kai ton peristasiakó bárbaro. Allá tóra ótan skotóno éna várvaro, koitázo to prósopó tou kai skéftomai, "Ísos den prépei na skotónoume aftoús tous anthrópous". / I thought being a soldier would easier, all I expected to do is stand around and kill a few mobs and the occasional barbarian. But now when I kill a barbarian, I look at his face and think, "Maybe we shouldn't be killing these people."

//v2;120;Skéftesai pára polý! Vgeíte éxo kai skotóse kana bárbaro gia ti Rómi. Tha mas skotósoun kai tha katastrépsoun ta spítia mas! Eínai móno asyneíditoi ágrioi. / You think too much! Go out and kill barbarians for Rome. They would kill us and destroy our homes! They are only uncivilized savages.

//v1;150;Synantísate aftoús tous anthrópous pou kirýttete na skotónete? Óchi, den échete, ísos eínai diaforetikoí apó aftó pou mas eípan. / Have you met these people that you are preaching to kill? No, you have not, maybe they are different from what we were told.
//v2;180;Pragmati, tha boroúsan na eínai polý cheiróteroi. / True, they could be much worse.
//v1;210;Den nomízo óti katalavaínete tis sképseis kai ta deiná pou pernáo. / I don't think you understand the thoughts and plight I'm going through.

//v2;240;Eímai stratiótis, óchi filósofos. Tha prépei na páte na prosefchitheíte sto Theó gia kathodígisi, kathós safós chreiázeste. / I'm a soldier, not a philosopher. You should go to pray to God for guidance as you clearly need some.
//v1;270;I prosefchí voithá se periódous psychikís krísis. Tha páo na proséfchomai tóra. / Praying does help in times of mental crisis. I'll go pray now.
//v2;300;Elpízo óti o Theós tha balei ti sýnchysi sou. / I hope God will end your confusion.
//v1;0;Elpízo óti den tha chreiasteí na vgoúme éxo kai na polemísoume opoiondípote várvaro ópote sýntoma. / I hope we don't have to go out and fight any barbarians anytime soon.

//v2;30;Ti? Eímaste stratiótes, i douleiá mas eínai na vgoúme éxo kai na skotósoume várvarous. Giatí tha beíte ston strató an den sas arései na agonízeste? / What? We are soldiers, our job is to go out and kill barbarians. Why would you join the army if you don't like fighting?

//v1;60;Skéftika óti o stratiótis tha ítan efkolóteros, to móno pou perímena na káno eínai na stamatíso kai na skotóso lígous óchlous kai to peristasiakó várvaro. Allá tóra ótan skotóno éna várvaro, koitázo to prósopó tou kai skéftomai, "Ísos den prépei na skotónoume aftoús tous anthrópous". / I thought being a soldier would easier, all I expected to do is stand around and kill a few mobs and the occasional barbarian. But now when I kill a barbarian, I look at his face and think, "Maybe we shouldn't be killing these people."

//v2;120;Skéftesai pára polý! Vgeíte éxo kai skotóste várvarous gia ti Rómi. Tha mas skotósoun kai tha katastrépsoun ta spítia mas! Eínai móno asyneíditoi ágrioi. / You think too much! Go out and kill barbarians for Rome. They would kill us and destroy our homes! They are only uncivilized savages.

//v1;150;Synantísate aftoús tous anthrópous pou kirýttete na skotónete? Óchi, den échete, ísos eínai diaforetikoí apó aftó pou mas eípan. / Have you met these people that you are preaching to kill? No, you have not, maybe they are different from what we were told.
//v2;180;Eínai alítheia óti tha boroúsan na eínai polý cheirótera. / True, they could be much worse.
//v1;210;Den nomízo óti katalavaínete tis sképseis kai ta deiná pou pernáo. / I don't think you understand the thoughts and plight I'm going through.

//v2;240;Eímai stratiótis, óchi filósofos. Tha prépei na páte na prosefchitheíte sto Theó gia kathodígisi, kathós safós chreiázeste kápoio. / I'm a soldier, not a philosopher. You should go to pray to God for guidance as you clearly need some.

//v1;270;Écho ídi kai den écho típota perissótero apó ton Theó. Ótan prosefchómoun, émeina me to ídio sympérasma ópos écho tóra. / I already have and I got nothing more from God. When I prayed, I was left with the same conclusion as I have now.

//v2;300;Ti? Échete afísei safós ton Theó gia na min sas po tin alítheia! Pigaínete píso stin prosefchí méchri na borésete na skotósete kai páli tous varvárous! / What? You clearly have forsaken God for Him to not to tell you the truth! Go back to praying until you can kill barbarians again!
//v1;330;Ísos aftó eínai to sympérasma pou o Theós símane gia ména na écho! Tha páo na proséfchomai tóra. / Maybe this is conclusion God meant for me to have!
//v2;360;Akoúgetai perissótero ópos o Theós thélei na syntaxiodotitheíte ... / Sounds more like God wants you to retire...

rows.raw: //* The part before the ";" is the title, after it the description

parts.body: Stranger
parts.job: uk|Stranger

parts.body: As a folk of trade we have to accept everyone. But we don't have to trust them.
parts.translation: Ми торгуємо зі всіми, але не кожному довіряемо.

parts.body: Familiarity
Lately, you are often seen in these Roman areas.
parts.translation: Останнім часом тебе часто видно на Римській землі.

parts.body: Known Face
parts.job: uk|Known Face

parts.body: Other Romans seem to have noticed you and they speak well of you! You don't seem to be a barbarian after all.
parts.job: uk|Other Romans seem to have noticed you and they speak well of you! You don't seem to be a barbarian after all.

parts.body: Regular Visitor
Xaire, $name! Nice to see you. How are things?
parts.job: uk|Xaire, $name! Nice to see you. How are things?

parts.body: Fellow Civilized Man
parts.job: uk|Fellow Civilized Man

parts.body: Ah, it's good to see that others outside of the Roman Empire can be civilized like us once in a while.
parts.job: uk|Ah, it's good to see that others outside of the Roman Empire can be civilized like us once in a while.

parts.body: Favourite Trader
parts.job: uk|Favourite Trader

parts.body: Everyone here is glad to see you. Have you anything to trade? Our trading relationship has helped both of us out.
parts.translation: Ми завжди раді тобі. Є товари для торгівлі?

parts.body: Friend of the Village
parts.job: uk|Friend of the Village

parts.body: You are part of our village $name, we trust you now!
parts.job: uk|You are part of our village $name, we trust you now!

parts.body: Respectable Ally
parts.job: uk|Respectable Ally

parts.body: Congrats $name! You have earned our respect. It's difficult for outsiders to become friends of the Roman Empire, let alone respected. But YOU, you have proven yourself worthy!
parts.job: uk|Congrats $name! You have earned our respect. It's difficult for outsiders to become friends of the Roman Empire, let alone respected. But YOU, you have proven yourself worthy!

parts.body: One of Us
parts.job: uk|One of Us

parts.body: We see you now as a Roman civic $name. Maybe you weren't born as one of us, but now you can be proud to call yourself a true Roman.
parts.job: uk|We see you now as a Roman civic $name. Maybe you weren't born as one of us, but now you can be proud to call yourself a true Roman.

parts.body: Natural Leader
$name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Byzantines. They will follow you anywhere.
parts.job: uk|$name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Byzantines. They will follow you anywhere.

parts.body: The Next Caesar
parts.job: uk|The Next Caesar

parts.body: You will be the next Caesar! The sheer amount of work you have done for this village is unimaginable and we will follow you in making this world a better place. Hail $name!
parts.job: uk|You will be the next Caesar! The sheer amount of work you have done for this village is unimaginable and we will follow you in making this world a better place. Hail $name!

parts.body: Nuisance
You aren't very nice, $name. Watch your step.
parts.job: uk|You aren't very nice, $name. Watch your step.

parts.body: Unpleasant Outsider
We accept traders, but not people like you. Be on guard.
parts.translation: Ми приймаємо торговців, але не таких як ви.

parts.body: Public Enemy
parts.job: uk|Public Enemy

parts.body: It was embarrassing of the whole Roman empire to let you alive. While you continue to enjoy to live, leave the Roman lands and never return.
parts.translation: Римська Імперія не заспокоїться поки Ви живі!

parts.body: Apparent Barbarian
parts.job: uk|Apparent Barbarian

parts.body: Do you not understand us? Fine, we'll try something else: BAR BAR BAR, BAR BAR, BAR BARRRR!
parts.job: uk|Do you not understand us? Fine, we'll try something else: BAR BAR BAR, BAR BAR, BAR BARRRR!

rows.raw: //For most villagers, greeting lines have not been added yet.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=$name! Gnorízeis óti oi Romaíoi eínai oi kalýteroi kataskevastés? /
parts.body: $name! Did you know that Romans are the best architects?
parts.job: uk|$name! Did you know that Romans are the best architects?

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=$name! Des pos ftiaxno ena architektoniko dimiourgima! /
parts.body: $name! Watch me build a beautiful structure.
parts.job: uk|$name! Watch me build a beautiful structure.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=Aftó to ktírio tha ginei poli ómorfo! /
parts.body: This building will be beautiful!
parts.job: uk|This building will be beautiful!

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=Den échei teliosei, allá vlépo tin omorfiá stin douleiá mou. /
parts.body: It's not done, but I already see the beauty in my work.
parts.job: uk|It's not done, but I already see the beauty in my work.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=Dimioúrgo tóso entiposiakes domés. I architektoniki eínai pragmatiká i pio ómorfi morfí téchnis./
parts.body: I build such elaborate structures. Building is truly the most beautiful form of art.
parts.job: uk|I build such elaborate structures. Building is truly the most beautiful form of art.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=I Rómi den chtístike se mia méra, chtístike toublo me toublo. /
parts.body: Rome wasn't built in a day, it was built block by block.
parts.job: uk|Rome wasn't built in a day, it was built block by block.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=I architektonikí mas eínai anóteri apó óla ta álla ktíria se olókliro ton kósmo. /
parts.body: Our architecture is superior to all other buildings across the world.
parts.job: uk|Our architecture is superior to all other buildings across the world.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=I oikodómisi me ton romaïkó trópo eínai o kalýteros trópos. /
parts.body: Building in the Roman way is the best way.
parts.job: uk|Building in the Roman way is the best way.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=Sas arései to tropos kataskeuis mou? /
parts.body: Do you like my style?
parts.job: uk|Do you like my style?

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.construction=Chtizo apo tote pou thymamai. I architektoniki échei gínei i zoí mou. /
parts.body: I've been building longer than I can remember. Building has become my life.
parts.job: uk|I've been building longer than I can remember. Building has become my life.

parts.body: Where does the village get these blocks from?
parts.job: uk|Where does the village get these blocks from?

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.getResourcesForBuild=Chreiázomai ylika gia na ftiáxo tis kalýteres kataskevés! /
parts.body: I need blocks to build the best structures!
parts.job: uk|I need blocks to build the best structures!

parts.body: Every build starts with the blocks.
parts.job: uk|Every build starts with the blocks.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.getResourcesForBuild=Prépei na epiléxo prosektiká ta ylika o ídios. /
parts.body: I must carefully select the blocks myself.
parts.job: uk|I must carefully select the blocks myself.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.getResourcesForBuild=Pós metaférete tósa pollá ylika ótan ftiáchnete $name? /
parts.body: How do you carry so many blocks when you build $name?
parts.job: uk|How do you carry so many blocks when you build $name?

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.getResourcesForBuild=To cheirótero méros tou ktiríou eínai na i metafora ton ylikon. /
parts.body: The worst part of building is getting the blocks.
parts.job: uk|The worst part of building is getting the blocks.

parts.body: Enough building! I need some wine!
parts.job: uk|Enough building! I need some wine!

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.goDrink=Chreiázomai éna potó gia na me empnéfsei! /
parts.body: I need a drink to inspire me!
parts.job: uk|I need a drink to inspire me!

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.goDrink=Káthe kalós oikodómos chreiázetai éna potó sto télos tis iméras. /
parts.body: Every good architect needs a drink at the end of the day.
parts.job: uk|Every good architect needs a drink at the end of the day.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.goDrink=I douleia mou fernei dipsa gia krasí. /
parts.body: Building makes me thirsty for wine.
parts.job: uk|Building makes me thirsty for wine.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gopray=Elpízo o Theós mou dínei émpnefsi gia to epómeno ktírio mou! /
parts.body: I hope God gives me inspiration for my next building!
parts.job: uk|I hope God gives me inspiration for my next building!

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gopray=Giatí o Theós me ékane architéktona? /
parts.body: Why did God make me an architect?
parts.job: uk|Why did God make me an architect?

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gopray=I prosefchí eínai éna simantikó méros tou romaïkoú ktiríou. /
parts.body: Praying is an important part of Roman building.
parts.job: uk|Praying is an important part of Roman building.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gopray=Katanoeí ta provlímata pou échoun oi architéktones. /
parts.body: He understands the troubles architects have.
parts.job: uk|He understands the troubles architects have.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gorest=An den koimithó, yparxei periptosi na kano palabomara. /
parts.body: If I do not sleep, I might mess up building something.
parts.job: uk|If I do not sleep, I might mess up building something.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gorest=Den boró na oikodomíso ótan eimai kourasmenos. /
parts.body: I cannot build when tired.
parts.job: uk|I cannot build when tired.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gorest=Eínai dýskolo na chtizei kaneis sto skotádi. /
parts.body: It is hard to build in the dark.
parts.job: uk|It is hard to build in the dark.

parts.body: I am done with building for the day.
parts.job: uk|I am done with building for the day.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gorest=Ísos tha oneireftó ta kalýtera ktíria ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Maybe I will dream of building the world's best buildings!
parts.job: uk|Maybe I will dream of building the world's best buildings!

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gosocialise=Kaneís se aftó to chorió den katalavaínei ta provlímata tis oikodómisis. /
parts.body: No one in this village understands the troubles of building.
parts.job: uk|No one in this village understands the troubles of building.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gosocialise=Káthe architéktonas chreiázetai émpnefsi apó állous. /
parts.body: Every architect needs inspiration from others.
parts.job: uk|Every architect needs inspiration from others.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gosocialise=Oi architéktones chreiázontai polles apopseis gia na evdokimísoun. /
parts.body: Architects need feedback to thrive.
parts.job: uk|Architects need feedback to thrive.

parts.prefix: architect_byzantine.gosocialise=Ti na skéftetai to chorió gia ta ktíriá mou? /
parts.body: What does the village think of my buildings?
parts.job: uk|What does the village think of my buildings?

parts.body: Do not attack anyone who uses my weapons.
parts.translation: Навіть не намагайтеся битися зі мною, я - ціла армія

parts.prefix: armysmith_byzantine.MakeByzantineMace=Aftó to ropalo steilei tous barbarous sto gamo tou karagkiozi! /
parts.body: This mace will launch barbarians far!
parts.job: uk|This mace will launch barbarians far!

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.greeting=$name, to chorió mou échei ta kalýtera emporévmata gia pólisi! /
parts.body: $name, my village has the best goods on sale!
parts.job: uk|$name, my village has the best goods on sale!

parts.body: Hello wealthy traveller!
parts.job: uk|Hello wealthy traveller!

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.greeting=Thélete na voithísete na parakolouthísete tous agrótes $name? /
parts.body: Do you want to help watch the peasants $name?
parts.job: uk|Do you want to help watch the peasants $name?

parts.body: Enough governing! I need a drink.
parts.job: uk|Enough governing! I need a drink.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.goDrink=Axízei na pio to kalýtero krasí! /
parts.body: I deserve to drink the best wine!
parts.job: uk|I deserve to drink the best wine!

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.goDrink=Prépei na elénxo an i tavérna eínai kerdofóra. /
parts.body: I should check if the tavern is profitable.
parts.job: uk|I should check if the tavern is profitable.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.goDrink=Káthe ischyró átomo prépei na piei í tha pethánei apó to ánchos! /
parts.body: Every powerful person needs to drink or they will die from the stress!
parts.job: uk|Every powerful person needs to drink or they will die from the stress!

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gopray=Giatí o Theós na me kanei Eparxo? /
parts.body: Why did God make me a baron?
parts.job: uk|Why did God make me a baron?

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gopray=I prosefchí eínai éna simantikó méros tis romaïkís kyvérnisis. /
parts.body: Praying is an important part of Roman governing.
parts.job: uk|Praying is an important part of Roman governing.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gopray=Katanoeí ta provlímata pou échoun oi Eparxoi. /
parts.body: He understands the troubles barons have.
parts.job: uk|He understands the troubles barons have.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gopray=To chorió mou chreiázetai apantíseis apó to Theó! /
parts.body: My village needs answers from God!
parts.job: uk|My village needs answers from God!

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gorest=Arketí diacheírisi ton agrotón! Chreiázomai lígo ýpno. /
parts.body: Enough managing the peasants! I need some sleep.
parts.job: uk|Enough managing the peasants! I need some sleep.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gorest=*Chasmouritó* Den boró na odigíso tous agrótes ótan eímai kourasménos. /
parts.body: *Yawn* I cannot lead peasants when I am tired.
parts.job: uk|*Yawn* I cannot lead peasants when I am tired.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gorest=Óra na koimithó sti metaxénia mou kouvérta. /
parts.body: Time to sleep in my silky blanket.
parts.job: uk|Time to sleep in my silky blanket.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gorest=Óloi chreiázontai ýpno, eidiká ótan eíste igétis enós chorioú. /
parts.body: Everyone needs sleep, especially when you are a leader of a village.
parts.job: uk|Everyone needs sleep, especially when you are a leader of a village.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gosocialise=Giatí oi anóitoi chorikoí vlépoun móno ton eaftó mou os ton "Eparxo"? /
parts.body: Why do the stupid peasants only view me as the "Baron"?
parts.job: uk|Why do the stupid peasants only view me as the "Baron"?

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gosocialise=Hm, as doúme an katévale tous fórous tou. /
parts.body: He he he, let's see if he paid his taxes.
parts.job: uk|He he he, let's see if he paid his taxes.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gosocialise=Óra na empnéfso tous ftochoús na kerdísoun kana denarion! /
parts.body: Time to inspire the poor to earn denier!
parts.job: uk|Time to inspire the poor to earn denier!

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gosocialise=Prépei na milíso me ton koinó laó? /
parts.body: Do I have to talk to the common folk?
parts.job: uk|Do I have to talk to the common folk?

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.gosocialise=Os Eparxos, prépei na milíso ston laó mou, akóma ki an den to thélo. /
parts.body: As baron, I have to talk to my people, even if I don't want to.
parts.job: uk|As baron, I have to talk to my people, even if I don't want to.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.inspectconstruction=Prépei na sigoureftó óti oi agrótes den ésfaxan káti. /
parts.body: I need to make sure that the peasants did not mess something up.
parts.job: uk|I need to make sure that the peasants did not mess something up.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.inspectconstruction=Aftó to ktírio tha férei kérdos sto chorió mou. /
parts.body: This building will bring profit to my village.
parts.job: uk|This building will bring profit to my village.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.inspectconstruction=I pragmatiki eutixia einai na vlépeis to chorió sou na ploutízei. /
parts.body: Beauty is watching your village get wealthier.
parts.job: uk|Beauty is watching your village get wealthier.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.inspectconstruction=Xéro óti i Rómi den chtístike se mia méra, allá giatí o architéktonas mou eínai tóso argós? /
parts.body: I know that Rome was not built in a day, but why is my architect being so slow?
parts.job: uk|I know that Rome was not built in a day, but why is my architect being so slow?

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.inspectconstruction=Eínai dikí mou douleiá na diasfalíso óti ta ktíria tha kataskevastoún sostá. /
parts.body: It's my job to make sure that buildings get built right.
parts.job: uk|It's my job to make sure that buildings get built right.

parts.prefix: baron_byzantine.inspectconstruction=Oi architéktones mou kánoun syníthos kalí douleiá, allá prépei pánta na tis elénxo. /
parts.body: My architects usually do a good job, but I need to always check up on them.
parts.job: uk|My architects usually do a good job, but I need to always check up on them.

parts.body: Time to become a strong man!
parts.job: uk|Time to become a strong man!

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.becomeAdult=Eímai arketá megálos gia na doulépso mia douleiá! /
parts.body: I am old enough to work a job!
parts.job: uk|I am old enough to work a job!

parts.body: I need a job now.
parts.job: uk|I need a job now.

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.becomeAdult=Oi méres mou na eímai agóri teleiónoun. /
parts.body: My days of being a boy are over.
parts.job: uk|My days of being a boy are over.

parts.body: I want to fight someone!
parts.job: uk|I want to fight someone!

parts.body: I want to play "Fight the Barbarian"!
parts.job: uk|I want to play "Fight the Barbarian"!

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.goPlay=Tha deíxo se ólous óti eímai megálos kai ischyrós! /
parts.body: I will show everyone that I am big and strong!
parts.job: uk|I will show everyone that I am big and strong!

parts.body: Time to play "soldier".
parts.job: uk|Time to play "soldier".

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.gopray=Thélo na mátho gia to Theó! /
parts.body: I want to learn about God!
parts.job: uk|I want to learn about God!

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.gopray=Boreí na mou pei o Theós gia tous enílikes? /
parts.body: Can God tell me about adults?
parts.job: uk|Can God tell me about adults?

parts.body: How do I pray?
parts.job: uk|How do I pray?

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.gopray=Den thélo na prosefchithó! Thélo na paíxo! /
parts.body: I do not want to pray! I want to play instead!
parts.job: uk|I do not want to pray! I want to play instead!

parts.prefix: boy_byzantine.childobservesmithing=Ótan megaló, thélo na eímai kimás epísis. Í énas stratiótis. Í énas stratigós! /
parts.body: When I grow up I want to be a smith also. Or a soldier. Or a general!
parts.job: uk|When I grow up I want to be a smith also. Or a soldier. Or a general!

parts.translation: Тут так нудно, ніколи нічого не відбувається ...

parts.prefix: keeperTropical_byzantine.greeting=Einai toso zesta edo. Den borw na katalavo giati aftoi 'Indian' zoun se afth th gh. /
parts.body: It's so hot here. I can't understand why those Indians live in these lands.
parts.translation: Вітаю вас, мандрівник, як же ви опинилися в наших краях?

parts.prefix: keeperTropical_byzantine.greeting=Exeis dei pote aftous tous periergous tous 'Maya' ? Ta ktiria tous moiazoun san na einai etoima na katareusoun. /
parts.body: Have you ever seen those strange Mayas? Their buildings look like they could collapse any second.
parts.translation: Тут так жарко. Я не можу зрозуміти, чому ці Хінді живуть в цих землях?

parts.prefix: keeperTropical_byzantine.greeting=Kalhspera taxideuth, anarwtiemai pws irthes ews edw. /
parts.body: Greetings traveller, I wonder how you ended up in this faraway place.
parts.translation: Ви коли-небудь бачили цих дивних Майя? Їх будівлі виглядають, як ніби вони можуть звалитися в будь-яку секунду.

parts.prefix: keeperTropical_byzantine.greeting=Pws skeftike kapios oti mporei na brei ergasia edw... /
parts.body: How could anyone think someone should be posted here...
parts.job: uk|How could anyone think someone should be posted here...

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.BringBackResourcesHome=As elpísoume óti aftó tha eínai arketó gia na evdokimísei to chorió! /
parts.body: Hopefully this will be enough for the village to thrive!
parts.translation: Моя дружина має пишатися мною і всієї тієї деревиною що я приніс.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.BringBackResourcesHome=Eímai polý epitychiménos xylourgós, i apografí mou eínai gemáti me koútsoura! /
parts.body: I am a very successful lumberman, my inventory is filled with logs!
parts.job: uk|I am a very successful lumberman, my inventory is filled with logs!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.BringBackResourcesHome=Férno pollá déntra allá den eínai variá gia kápoio lógo. /
parts.body: I am carrying many trees but they aren't heavy for some reason.
parts.job: uk|I am carrying many trees but they aren't heavy for some reason.

parts.body: That was a job well done.
parts.job: uk|That was a job well done.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.BringBackResourcesHome=H gynaika mou prepei na einai perhfanh me olo to xilo pou efera . /
parts.body: My wife must be proud with all the wood I have brought.
parts.job: uk|My wife must be proud with all the wood I have brought.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Kathe ktirio edw xreiazete xilo, h apokthsh tou einai douleia mou! /
parts.body: Every structure here needs wood, and getting it is my job!
parts.translation: Для кожної споруди потрібно дерево і добувати його - моя робота!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Éna állo déntro káto, perissótero xýlo gia to chorió! /
parts.body: Another tree down, more wood for the village!
parts.job: uk|Another tree down, more wood for the village!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Éna állo déntro káto, perissótero xýlo gia to chorió! /
parts.body: One more tree down, more wood for the village!
parts.job: uk|One more tree down, more wood for the village!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=$name, échete kópsei poté éna déntro prin? /
parts.body: $name, have you ever chopped down a tree before?
parts.job: uk|$name, have you ever chopped down a tree before?

parts.body: Get to the Choppa tree!
parts.job: uk|Get to the Choppa tree!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Pethaínoun déntro pethaínoun! CHACHACHA! Kaloúpi! Kaloúpi! Kaloúpi! CHA-O, Geia sou, $name! Típota ... paráxeno ... symvaínei edó.! /
parts.body: Die tree die! HAHAHA! Die! Die! Die! Ha- Oh, hi there $name! Nothing.. strange... happening here.
parts.job: uk|Die tree die! HAHAHA! Die! Die! Die! Ha- Oh, hi there $name! Nothing.. strange... happening here.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Den thélo na se skotóso, allá prépei na ... Antío déntro! /
parts.body: I don't want to kill you, but I have to... Goodbye tree!
parts.job: uk|I don't want to kill you, but I have to... Goodbye tree!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Échete anarotitheí poté giatí ta temachisména déntra ftánoun edó, $name? Eínai polý períergo. Ó, ti ki an káno, pántote epipléoun kai prépei na spáso to déntro pros ta páno lígo sigá, eínai énas tétoios pónos.! /
parts.body: Have you ever wondered why chopped down trees float here, $name? It's very strange. No matter what I do, they always float and I have to break the tree upward bit by bit, it's such a pain.
parts.job: uk|Have you ever wondered why chopped down trees float here, $name? It's very strange. No matter what I do, they always float and I have to break the tree upward bit by bit, it's such a pain.

parts.body: Hey $name! Don't take that!
parts.job: uk|Hey $name! Don't take that!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Ta déntra megálosan kalá aftí ti forá, tósa pollá koútsoura kai fytá. /
parts.body: The trees grew well this time, so many logs and saplings.
parts.job: uk|The trees grew well this time, so many logs and saplings.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Elpízo óti to chorió tha chreiasteí óla aftá ta koútsoura. /
parts.body: I hope the village needs all of these logs.
parts.job: uk|I hope the village needs all of these logs.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Aftó ítan éna megálo déntro! Tóra to chorió boreí na chrisimopoiísei ta koútsourá tou. /
parts.body: That was one big tree! Now the village can use its logs.
parts.job: uk|That was one big tree! Now the village can use its logs.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Koitáxte óla aftá ta néa kormoús kai ta fytá pou píra apó tin kopí ton déntron! /
parts.body: Look at all of these new logs and saplings I got from chopping down the trees!
parts.job: uk|Look at all of these new logs and saplings I got from chopping down the trees!

parts.body: Nice sapling over there.
parts.job: uk|Nice sapling over there.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Aftá ta fytá eínai tóso mikrá, merikés forés den boró na pistépso óti tha gínoun tóso megála. /
parts.body: These saplings are so small, sometimes I can't believe that they will become so big.
parts.translation: Незабаром це буде велике, величне дерево! І я зрубаю його.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Eísai tóso charitoméno mikrófyllo, schedón me afínei na xecháso óti tha se kópso ótan megalóseis. /
parts.body: You're so cute little sapling, almost lets me forget I'm going to chop you down when you grow up.
parts.job: uk|You're so cute little sapling, almost lets me forget I'm going to chop you down when you grow up.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=$name, thélete na fytépsete éna fytó? /
parts.body: $name, do you want to plant a sapling?
parts.job: uk|$name, do you want to plant a sapling?

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Ta déntra megalónoun tóso grígora edó, se líges méres gyrízoun apó aftó to mikroskopikó déntro méchri na eínai éna gemáto déntro. /
parts.body: Trees grow so fast here, in a few days they turn from this tiny sapling to being a full tree.
parts.job: uk|Trees grow so fast here, in a few days they turn from this tiny sapling to being a full tree.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=I fýtefsi eínai i efkolóteri douleiá, to móno pou prépei na káno eínai na ta topothetíso sto édafos. /
parts.body: Planting is the easiest job, all I have to do is place them on the ground.
parts.job: uk|Planting is the easiest job, all I have to do is place them on the ground.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Syntoma tha ginei ena megalo, panemorfo dentro! Kai tha to kopsw.  /
parts.body: Soon this will be a big, majestic tree! And I'll cut it down.
parts.job: uk|Soon this will be a big, majestic tree! And I'll cut it down.

parts.prefix: merchant_art.greeting=Kamía póli ston kósmo den boreí na synkritheí me tin omorfiá kai ti dýnami tis Konstantinoúpolis. /
parts.body: No city in the world can compare with the beauty and might of Constantinople.
parts.translation: Жодне місто в світі не може зрівнятися з Константинополем.

parts.body: We are the last true Romans!
parts.translation: Ми - Візантійці, останні з істинних Римлян.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=I douleiá mou eínai na spáso ta vráchia kai na metatrépso aftá ta vráchia pros epexergasía, aftó eínai. /
parts.body: My job is to break rocks and take those rocks to be smelted, that's it.
parts.translation: У цій роботі сила і витривалість необхідні. Але тут ніхто цього не помічає ...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=To chéri mou ponáei apó ti chrísi aftís tis pikkáx káthe méra. /
parts.body: My arm hurts from using this pickaxe every day.
parts.translation: Я гордий бути римським громадянином, працюючим на славу Імперії, навіть на такій важкій роботі.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Éna blok, dýo blok, tría blok, téssera blok, den teleiónei poté. Akrivós to ídio prágma xaná kai xaná. /
parts.body: One block, two block, three block, four block, it never ends. Just the same thing over and over again.
parts.job: uk|One block, two block, three block, four block, it never ends. Just the same thing over and over again.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Éna blok, dýo blok, treis anamonís, eínai aftós o chrysós? Aftó eínai? Vríka to chrysó! CHRYSOS! CHRYSOS! Eímai ploúsios! HAHA-ítan aplá sidírou pou antanaklá se kakó fos. Epistrofí sto exóryxi sidírou kai ánthraka ... /
parts.body: One block, two block, three-wait, is that gold?  That is? I FOUND GOLD! GOLD! GOLD! I'm rich! HAHA-oh, it was just iron reflecting in a bad light. Back to mining iron and coal...
parts.job: uk|One block, two block, three-wait, is that gold?  That is? I FOUND GOLD! GOLD! GOLD! I'm rich! HAHA-oh, it was just iron reflecting in a bad light. Back to mining iron and coal...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Ogdónta blok, ogdónta éna blok, októ dýo blok, ogdónta tría blok ... /
parts.body: Eighty block, eighty one block, eight two block, eighty three block...
parts.job: uk|Eighty block, eighty one block, eight two block, eighty three block...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Geia sou! Pós metaféroun tósa pollá blok kai i dikí mou tóso grígora? Chreiázontai óres gia na káno aftó pou káneis se mia méra. /
parts.body: Hey! How do you carry so many blocks and mine so fast? It takes me hours to do what you do in a day.
parts.job: uk|Hey! How do you carry so many blocks and mine so fast? It takes me hours to do what you do in a day.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=*ghouch* *Ghouch*, misó na ergázomai me ánthraka. /
parts.body: *Cough* *Cough*, I hate working with coal.
parts.job: uk|*Cough* *Cough*, I hate working with coal.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Gia na kaneis aythn thn douleia h dynamh kai h antoxh einai aparaithta. Kaneis omws den to katalabainei... /
parts.body: In this job strength and endurance is needed. But nobody here notices...
parts.job: uk|In this job strength and endurance is needed. But nobody here notices...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Eimai perifanos pou eimai Romaios katoikos kai pou douleyw gia thn aytokratoria , an kai einai dyskolh douleia. /
parts.body: I'm proud to be a Roman Citizen working for the glorious Empire, even in this hard job.
parts.job: uk|I'm proud to be a Roman Citizen working for the glorious Empire, even in this hard job.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.makebooks=Ta biblia mou einai merika apo ta kalytera xeirografa ekei exo. /
parts.body: My books are some of the best manuscripts out there.
parts.translation: Мої книги є одними з кращих рукописів за межами Візантії.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=Giatí o Theós me ékane énan apó tous pio polýtimous ypirétes tou? /
parts.body: Why did God make me one of his most treasured servants?
parts.job: uk|Why did God make me one of his most treasured servants?

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=Os Patriárchis, prépei na odigíso tin prosefchí. /
parts.body: As the Patriarch, I must lead the prayer.
parts.job: uk|As the Patriarch, I must lead the prayer.

parts.body: I understand the troubles He has.
parts.job: uk|I understand the troubles He has.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=Katanoeí ta provlímata pou échoun oi patriárches. /
parts.body: He understands the troubles patriarchs have.
parts.job: uk|He understands the troubles patriarchs have.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=To chorió mou chreiázetai apantíseis apó to Theó! /
parts.body: My village needs answers from God!
parts.job: uk|My village needs answers from God!

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gorest=Óloi chreiázontai ýpno, eidiká ótan eíste igétis enós chorioú. /
parts.body: Everyone needs sleep, especially when you are a leader of a village.
parts.job: uk|Everyone needs sleep, especially when you are a leader of a village.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gorest=*Chasmouritó* Den boró na odigíso tous iereís ótan eímai kourasménos./
parts.body: *Yawn* I cannot lead priests when I am tired.
parts.job: uk|*Yawn* I cannot lead priests when I am tired.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.inspectconstruction=I omorfiá vlépei to chorió sas na plisiázei perissótero sto Theó. /
parts.body: Beauty is watching your village get closer to God.
parts.job: uk|Beauty is watching your village get closer to God.

parts.prefix: pastor_byzantine.makebooks=Ta biblia mou einai merika apo ta kalytera xeirografa ekei exo. /
parts.body: My books are some of the best manuscripts out there.
parts.translation: Мої книги є одними з кращих рукописів за межами Візантії.

rows.raw: //smith_byzantine.MakeIndianTools=Ta romaïkós ergaleia einai ta kalytera ston kosmo. / Roman tools are the best in world.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=Énas kalós sideras prépei na proséfchetai káthe forá kai lígo. /
parts.body: A good smith needs to pray every once and a while.
parts.job: uk|A good smith needs to pray every once and a while.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=Giatí o Theós me ékane éna sídera? /
parts.body: Why did God make me a smith?
parts.job: uk|Why did God make me a smith?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=I prosefchí eínai éna simantikó méros tis romaïkís cheirotechnías. /
parts.body: Praying is an important part of Roman crafting.
parts.job: uk|Praying is an important part of Roman crafting.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=Katanoeí ta provlímata pou échoun oi siderades. /
parts.body: He understands the troubles smiths have.
parts.job: uk|He understands the troubles smiths have.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gorest=Ávrio tha káno pio ómorfa prágmata! /
parts.body: Tomorrow I will craft more beautiful things!
parts.job: uk|Tomorrow I will craft more beautiful things!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gorest=Écho kánei me ktírio gia tin iméra. /
parts.body: I am done with crafting for the day.
parts.job: uk|I am done with crafting for the day.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gorest=Ísos tha oneireftó na káno ta kalýtera ergaleía ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Maybe I will dream of crafting the world's best tools!
parts.job: uk|Maybe I will dream of crafting the world's best tools!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gosocialise=Tha zitíso na do an kápoios chreiázetai na kataskeváso káti. /
parts.body: I will ask to see if anyone needs me to craft something.
parts.job: uk|I will ask to see if anyone needs me to craft something.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gosocialise=Elpízo óti to chorió ektimá ta ergaleía mou. /
parts.body: I hope that the village appreciates my tools.
parts.job: uk|I hope that the village appreciates my tools.

parts.body: Enough crafting! I need some wine!
parts.job: uk|Enough crafting! I need some wine!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.goDrink=Chreiázomai éna potó gia na me empnéfsei! /
parts.body: I need a drink to inspire me!
parts.job: uk|I need a drink to inspire me!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.goDrink=Káthe kalós siderás chreiázetai éna potó sto télos tis iméras. /
parts.body: Every good blacksmith needs a drink at the end of the day.
parts.job: uk|Every good blacksmith needs a drink at the end of the day.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.goDrink=I cheirotechnía me kánei na dipsá gia to krasí. /
parts.body: Crafting makes me thirsty for wine.
parts.job: uk|Crafting makes me thirsty for wine.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelaxe=Den boreíte na kópsete ta déntra chorís tsekoúri! /
parts.body: You cannot chop down trees without an axe!
parts.job: uk|You cannot chop down trees without an axe!

parts.body: I craft amazing axes.
parts.job: uk|I craft amazing axes.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelaxe=Oi romaïkoí áxones eínai merikoí apó tous kalýterous ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman axes are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: uk|Roman axes are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelaxe=Oi xylourgoí chreiázontai na kánoume tous áxonés tous. /
parts.body: The lumbermen need us to craft their axes.
parts.job: uk|The lumbermen need us to craft their axes.

parts.body: How do you craft your axes $name?
parts.job: uk|How do you craft your axes $name?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Den boreíte na ekmetallefteíte chorís ergaleía kalliérgeias! /
parts.body: You cannot farm without farming tools!
parts.job: uk|You cannot farm without farming tools!

parts.body: I craft amazing farming tools.
parts.job: uk|I craft amazing farming tools.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Romaïká ergaleía kalliérgeias eínai meriká apó ta kalýtera ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman farming tools are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: uk|Roman farming tools are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Oi agrótes chreiázontai na kataskevásoume ta ergaleía tous. /
parts.body: The farmers need us to craft their tools.
parts.job: uk|The farmers need us to craft their tools.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Pós dimiourgeíte ta georgiká sas ergaleía $name? /
parts.body: How do you craft your farming tools $name?
parts.job: uk|How do you craft your farming tools $name?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelpickaxe=Den boreíte na to dikí sas chorís pickaxe! /
parts.body: You cannot mine without a pickaxe!
parts.job: uk|You cannot mine without a pickaxe!

parts.body: I craft strong pickaxes.
parts.job: uk|I craft strong pickaxes.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelpickaxe=Ta romaïká pickaxes eínai meriká apó ta kalýtera ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman pickaxes are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: uk|Roman pickaxes are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelpickaxe=Oi anthrakorýchoi mas chreiázontai na kataskevásoume ta pickaxes tous. /
parts.body: The miners need us to craft their pickaxes.
parts.job: uk|The miners need us to craft their pickaxes.

parts.body: How do you craft your pickaxes $name?
parts.job: uk|How do you craft your pickaxes $name?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelshovel=Den boreíte na chtísete í na skápsete chorís éna ftyári! /
parts.body: You cannot build or dig without a shovel!
parts.job: uk|You cannot build or dig without a shovel!

parts.body: I craft durable shovels.
parts.job: uk|I craft durable shovels.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelshovel=Romaïká ftyária eínai meriká apó ta kalýtera ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman shovels are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: uk|Roman shovels are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelshovel=Oi architéktones chreiázontai na kataskevásoume ta ftyária tous. /
parts.body: The architects need us to craft their shovels.
parts.job: uk|The architects need us to craft their shovels.

parts.body: How do you craft your shovels $name?
parts.job: uk|How do you craft your shovels $name?

parts.body: Hello, $name!
parts.job: uk|Hello, $name!

parts.body: Beautiful day, isn't it?
parts.job: uk|Beautiful day, isn't it?

parts.body: It will rain soon.
parts.job: uk|It will rain soon.

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Kamia polh ston kosmo den sygrinete me tin Konstantinoúpoli./
parts.body: No city in the world can compare with Constantinople.
parts.translation: Немає такого міста у світі, що міг би зрівнятися з Константинополем.

parts.body: We aren't Greek, we're Roman.
parts.job: uk|We aren't Greek, we're Roman.

parts.body: We are the last true Romans.
parts.translation: Ми - Візантійці, останні з істинних Римлян. Грійтеся в променях нашої слави.

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Varéli sti dóxa tou politismoú mas katá ti diárkeia tis paramonís sas edó. /
parts.body: Bask in the glory of our civilization during your stay here.
parts.job: uk|Bask in the glory of our civilization during your stay here.

parts.body: Welcome to the village, $name!
parts.job: uk|Welcome to the village, $name!

parts.body: Look! There's $name!
parts.job: uk|Look! There's $name!

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Eimaste oi Byzantinoi, oi teleutaioi alhthinoi Romaioi. Ypoklitheite stin doxa tou politismou mas. /
parts.body: We are the last true Romans. Bath in the light of our civilisation.
parts.job: uk|We are the last true Romans. Bath in the light of our civilisation.

parts.body: Finally, I have become a Roman citizen!

parts.prefix: villager.huntmonster=Prépei na skotóso aftón ton bárbaro! /
parts.body: I need to kill this barbarian!
parts.job: uk|I need to kill this barbarian!

parts.body: I think I'll go play outside.
parts.job: uk|I think I'll go play outside.

parts.body: I will go play now.
parts.job: uk|I will go play now.

parts.prefix: villager.goPlay=$name! Théleis na paíxeis mazí mou? /
parts.body: $name! Do you want to play with me?
parts.job: uk|$name! Do you want to play with me?

parts.body: I want to run!
parts.job: uk|I want to run!

parts.body: The Roman Empire is attacked! To arms!
parts.translation: Римська Імперія під атакою! До зброї!

parts.body: The barbarians are here! Defend our village at all costs!
parts.job: uk|The barbarians are here! Defend our village at all costs!

parts.prefix: villager.childeatgrapes=Orkízomai óti aftá ta stafýlia épesan mónoi tous! /
parts.body: I swear these grapes fell on their own!
parts.job: uk|I swear these grapes fell on their own!

parts.body: Millénaire adds <darkblue>villages<black> from different cultures to  Minecraft. Those villages are randomly generated in different biomes. They are of different styles and offer different products, but they all have a chief, construct new buildings, trade with you and like you or not depending on your actions (see the "reputation" section).

parts.body: <darkblue>Frequently Asked Questions
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Frequently Asked Questions

parts.body: <darkblue>The villagers speak in a language other than mine. Is this normal?
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>The villagers speak in a language other than mine. Is this normal?

parts.body: Millénaire villagers all speak in "their" language, such as Hindi for the Indians or French for the Normans. If you play in a different language, you will "learn" the language by interacting with them (trade, quests ...). As you “learn” their language, Millénaire will provide translations, first of the names of buildings, then of the types of villagers, and finally of the villager dialogues.
parts.job: uk|Millénaire villagers all speak in "their" language, such as Hindi for the Indians or French for the Normans. If you play in a different language, you will "learn" the language by interacting with them (trade, quests ...). As you “learn” their language, Millénaire will provide translations, first of the names of buildings, then of the types of villagers, and finally of the villager dialogues.

parts.body: <darkblue>Commerce
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Commerce

parts.body: Your most common exchanges with the villagers will be trading - you can sell many goods to them, and in return buy products, including blocks and objects specific to Millénaire. To trade with a village, go to the main building (or another store) and wait for a villager to come and see you with "Selling to the player" showing above his head. parts.body: <darkblue>Reputation & village chief
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Reputation & village chief

parts.body: Each village in Millénaire has a opinion of you, neutral at the start and changing according to your actions. This reputation is very important: many rewards are only possible with a good reputation, and if your reputation gets too bad, villagers can refuse to trade with you. You can check your reputation by speaking (<darkblue>right-click<black>) with the village chief.
parts.job: uk|Each village in Millénaire has a opinion of you, neutral at the start and changing according to your actions. This reputation is very important: many rewards are only possible with a good reputation, and if your reputation gets too bad, villagers can refuse to trade with you. You can check your reputation by speaking (<darkblue>right-click<black>) with the village chief.

parts.body: The main way to improve your reputation is to trade with the village. Purchases as well as sales improve your reputation in proportion to the price. You can also improve your reputation by performing quests for them. Conversely, attacking a village or failling certain missions will damage your reputation.

parts.body: You also have a <darkblue>reputation with each culture<black>. This reputation is affected by all your dealings with villages of this culture, and affects your trading with all other villages of the same culture. For example, if you have a very good reputation with a Norman village, other Norman villages will also like you (a little) more. You can check your reputation with every culture in the information screen (“M” key by default).

parts.body: <darkblue>Village expansion
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Village expansion

parts.body: All villages start off small around a central building (of varying nature: fort, palace, monastery, etc ... commonly referred to as the "town hall"), with a few houses or other buildings. The villagers' main goal is to expand their village by selecting new buildings to build and improvements to existing buildings. For that reason, they need resources - they can produce some themselves (lumbermen harvest wood, and miners stone ...) but depend on the player for others. Their material needs for the planned construction are displayed in the main building. You can help by selling these resources first.

For that reason, they need resources - they can produce some themselves (lumbermen harvest wood, and miners stone ...) but depend on the player for others. parts.body: The village population will also increase over time - at night, married villagers can have children. Once grown, these children move into new homes if available and become adults.

parts.body: The expansion of a village will cease in general two ways: either because the village has completed all buildable structures, or because it has no place. In the latter case, you can look at the village map to see which areas are unbuildable. It is sometimes possible to make them buildable, for example by filling in a lake.

parts.body: <darkblue>Combat and raiding
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Combat and raiding

parts.body: Millénaire is not always a peaceful mod: you can fight villagers, villages may conduct raids against each other, monsters can attack villages, and some isolated buildings are occupied by bandits. Whatever the circumstances, certain principles do not change: <darkblue>villagers are vulnerable only to direct attacks (melee, arrows and potions)<black>. They are not affected by fire, fall damage, or cactus. This restriction is intended to prevent the player from killing them without them being aware that the player is attacking them.

They are not affected by fire, fall damage, or cactus. This restriction is intended to prevent the player from killing them without them being aware that the player is attacking them.

parts.body: Villagers vary in strength, and the equipment they wear can make them much more dangerous.

parts.body: <darkblue>Respawning of villagers
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Respawning of villagers

parts.body: Once killed, a villager is temporarily dead. Dead villagers are respawned in their homes (but they will lose their equipment). After all, the player can respawn as well...

parts.body: <darkblue>Attack by players
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Attack by players

parts.body: You can always attack a villager, but other men of the village will then help to fight you. Should you manage to kill all the villagers of a village or lone building, the village's coffers will open and you can steal their contents.

parts.body: <darkblue>Bandits
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Bandits

parts.body: Some inhabitants of lone buildings will attack you without warning if you approach. Your reputation with their culture will not drop if you kill them. Like other villagers, they respawn at night - look under "<darkblue>destroy a village<black>" to see how to prevent it.

parts.body: <darkblue>Raids between villages
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Raids between villages

parts.body: Millénaire villages have positive or negative relations with nearby villages. These relations change randomly and may be influenced by the player talking to the chiefs of any of the villages. If their relations are very bad and one of the villages has enough fighters, it can launch a raid on other villages. You will be notified by a message. During a raid, the fighters attacking the town will be trying to kill the menfolk of the village they are attacking. If they do, they will take some of the resources as spoils. You can help one side or the other during a raid.

You can help one side or the other during a raid.

parts.body: It may be useful to encourage a village that you like to attack its neighbours to increase its resources. More cynically, encouraging raids can also allow you to help yourself to some of the loot once the defencers are dead.

parts.body: <darkblue>Hiring a villager
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Hiring a villager

parts.body: It is possible to hire some villagers such as the soldiers and lumbermen to help you in battles. They will follow and fight your enemies with you.

parts.body: <darkblue>Spawning villages
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Spawning villages

parts.body: You can spawn a village type of your choice to the location of your choice with a Summoning Wand, an object that you can buy in any village whenever you have a sufficiently high reputation. To use the wand, put a gold block where you want to spawn a village and right-click the block with the wand. The subsequent screen allows you to choose the desired type of village.

To use the wand, put a gold block where you want to spawn a village and right-click the block with the wand. The subsequent screen allows you to choose the desired type of village.

parts.body: <darkblue>Destruction of a village or lone building
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Destruction of a village or lone building

parts.body: The inhabitants of a village or building respawn every night, even if you destroy all the buildings in the village. To prevent this (if you want to occupy the buildings yourself, for example), you must use the <darkblue>Wand of Negation<black>: you will find it in the chests of the main building once all the inhabitants are dead. Please note that the destruction of a village is irreversible.

parts.body: <darkblue>Player-controlled Villages
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Player-controlled Villages

parts.body: It is possible to create a village with you as the leader, in which you can pick the locations of the buildings. To do this, you need to either be recognised as a leader in the culture of the village or to have completed the Creation Quest (see quests section), or to have increased your reputation to "natural leader" in a village and talk to its leader. You will then see an option to create player-controlled villages in the interface of the Summoning Wand.

You will then see an option to create player-controlled villages in the interface of the Summoning Wand.

parts.body: In player-controlled villages, you can order the construction of a new building using the wand at the desired location. An interface will open to allow you to choose the desired building. You can also allow or stop improvements to existing buildings via the "projects" panels. Trading resources with the villagers is unnecessary in these villages - just place items in the chests.

parts.body: <darkblue>Quests
parts.job: uk|<darkblue>Quests

parts.body: Quests are additional tasks that you can perform for the villagers. When a quest is available, it will be displayed above the head of a villager within square brackets, for example: "<darkblue>[Thirsty!]<black>." Right-click on it for a description of the task and the ability to accept or decline. Quests will be rewarded with money, reputation or objects. Some quests require you to have a good reputation with the village to be available.

parts.body: This special collection includes many missions and has two independent chapters, focusing on the Norman and Indian cultures. The first mission of each chapter will be assigned to you by an Indian or Norman villager once you have reached the reputation level of "Friend of the village" (the quest starts randomly, so it may take some time before the quest is available) .

parts.body: Both quests require you to find a special lone building. You must explore until you find it; be careful as it is very rare. Unlike other isolated buildings, however, these buildings appear when you use the "V" key.

parts.body: Is it snowing?
parts.job: uk|Is it snowing?

parts.body: It looks like snow, but doesn't seem to be cold.
parts.job: uk|It looks like snow, but doesn't seem to be cold.

parts.body: Where are we, this is not anywhere I have seen before. It looks the same but feels different.
parts.job: uk|Where are we, this is not anywhere I have seen before. It looks the same but feels different.

parts.body: The shamans say we are in the blessed land of the helpful spirits, that is why it is so amazing here!
parts.job: uk|The shamans say we are in the blessed land of the helpful spirits, that is why it is so amazing here!

parts.body: I'm tired, today is going by not fast enough...
parts.job: uk|I'm tired, today is going by not fast enough...

parts.body: Do you think the hunt will be good this year?
parts.job: uk|Do you think the hunt will be good this year?

parts.body: Who knows, with the weather we've had.
parts.job: uk|Who knows, with the weather we've had.

parts.body: Seasons don't make sense here.
parts.job: uk|Seasons don't make sense here.

parts.body: I met some weird people, they call themselves Normans?
parts.job: uk|I met some weird people, they call themselves Normans?

parts.body: Yeah the Normans are great but they sure need a lot.
parts.job: uk|Yeah the Normans are great but they sure need a lot.

parts.body: What do you mean?
parts.job: uk|What do you mean?

parts.body: One came by the other day and I emptied my house giving him stuff, he just kept needing more apparently.
parts.job: uk|One came by the other day and I emptied my house giving him stuff, he just kept needing more apparently.

parts.body: Poor guy.
parts.job: uk|Poor guy.

parts.body: Those Japanese people sure know how to prepare fish!
parts.job: uk|Those Japanese people sure know how to prepare fish!

parts.body: "Prepare" fish? You just mean they cook it, right?
parts.job: uk|"Prepare" fish? You just mean they cook it, right?

parts.body: No, I mean they serve their food with all of these elaborate methods and flavors.
parts.job: uk|No, I mean they serve their food with all of these elaborate methods and flavors.

parts.body: Food can taste different without just being spoiled?
parts.job: uk|Food can taste different without just being spoiled?

parts.body: Yeah you should come with me next time I check them out!
parts.job: uk|Yeah you should come with me next time I check them out!

parts.body: Did you hear what happened to him after the accident?
parts.job: uk|Did you hear what happened to him after the accident?

parts.body: Accident or not, killing people is wrong.
parts.job: uk|Accident or not, killing people is wrong.

parts.body: Yeah but did we need to kick him out of the village? I hear he has gone crazy on his own.
parts.job: uk|Yeah but did we need to kick him out of the village? I hear he has gone crazy on his own.

parts.body: We had to! At least here it isn't cold and he won't freeze to death out there.
parts.job: uk|We had to! At least here it isn't cold and he won't freeze to death out there.

parts.body: Is that better? Now he is forced to live alone by himself!
parts.job: uk|Is that better? Now he is forced to live alone by himself!

parts.body: When is the elder going to leave to die?
parts.job: uk|When is the elder going to leave to die?

parts.body: I don't think we need to do that here, this new world is much more accomodating!
parts.job: uk|I don't think we need to do that here, this new world is much more accomodating!

parts.body: I guess... but it is weird to see her still alive.
parts.job: uk|I guess... but it is weird to see her still alive.

parts.body: This place is weird, it is full of strange people.
parts.job: uk|This place is weird, it is full of strange people.

parts.body: You mean like $name?
parts.job: uk|You mean like $name?

parts.body: Well $name is just one person though, I mean all those others.
parts.job: uk|Well $name is just one person though, I mean all those others.
