parts.body: Have you heard what the elder says about those tall, slim, scary people?
parts.job: uk|Have you heard what the elder says about those tall, slim, scary people?

parts.body: What that they are the Shadow-People? I don't know...
parts.job: uk|What that they are the Shadow-People? I don't know...

parts.body: It makes sense though! If we are truly in a blessed land they would be twisted like that!
parts.job: uk|It makes sense though! If we are truly in a blessed land they would be twisted like that!

parts.body: But if we are in a blessed land then why are the Shadow-People even here?
parts.job: uk|But if we are in a blessed land then why are the Shadow-People even here?

parts.body: Oh... ummm, I don't know...
parts.job: uk|Oh... ummm, I don't know...

parts.body: I like snow.
parts.job: uk|I like snow.

parts.body: Good thing for an Inuit!
parts.job: uk|Good thing for an Inuit!

parts.body: I think our meat stores are running low, I hate when we run out.
parts.job: uk|I think our meat stores are running low, I hate when we run out.

parts.body: Meat is just not the same as stews...
parts.job: uk|Meat is just not the same as stews...

parts.body: But most stews have meat in them?
parts.job: uk|But most stews have meat in them?

parts.body: Yeah, but it just isn't the same...
parts.job: uk|Yeah, but it just isn't the same...

parts.body: Where are all the caribou? I miss caribou meat.
parts.job: uk|Where are all the caribou? I miss caribou meat.

parts.body: We have had many hunts, but none have found any caribou.
parts.job: uk|We have had many hunts, but none have found any caribou.

parts.body: We have found plenty of what looks like bison though!
parts.job: uk|We have found plenty of what looks like bison though!

parts.body: Yuck, I hate bison, caribou is better.
parts.job: uk|Yuck, I hate bison, caribou is better.

parts.body: Well then have the fish, we have lots of that.
parts.job: uk|Well then have the fish, we have lots of that.

parts.body: There isn't much to do around here.
parts.job: uk|There isn't much to do around here.

parts.body: It's good, peaceful.
parts.job: uk|It's good, peaceful.

parts.body: And boring...
parts.job: uk|And boring...

parts.body: You could dig a hole, or build a snow igloo!
parts.job: uk|You could dig a hole, or build a snow igloo!

parts.body: My own snow igloo?!
parts.job: uk|My own snow igloo?!

parts.body: I envy the shamans, wish I could speak with the spirits like they do.
parts.job: uk|I envy the shamans, wish I could speak with the spirits like they do.

parts.body: You could see if the shaman will teach you?
parts.job: uk|You could see if the shaman will teach you?

parts.body: Maybe... but some spirits are scary.
parts.job: uk|Maybe... but some spirits are scary.

parts.body: Right, there will always be scary spirits to watch out for.
parts.job: uk|Right, there will always be scary spirits to watch out for.

parts.body: My dad is much stronger than yours.
parts.job: uk|My dad is much stronger than yours.

parts.body: My dad is the strongest in the village dummy!
parts.job: uk|My dad is the strongest in the village dummy!

parts.body: Dream on. My dad can beat yours in two minutes flat.
parts.job: uk|Dream on. My dad can beat yours in two minutes flat.

parts.body: So beauty, what are you doing tonight?
parts.job: uk|So beauty, what are you doing tonight?

parts.body: $targetfirstname, I already told you, I am promised to another!
parts.job: uk|$targetfirstname, I already told you, I am promised to another!

parts.body: I've improved my skills again.
parts.job: uk|I've improved my skills again.

parts.body: You're quickly becoming a great hunter!
parts.job: uk|You're quickly becoming a great hunter!

parts.body: You really think so?
parts.job: uk|You really think so?

parts.body: I love the smell of meat cooking from the food preparer.
parts.job: uk|I love the smell of meat cooking from the food preparer.

parts.body: I don't know I usually prefer my meat uncooked, it changes the taste.
parts.job: uk|I don't know I usually prefer my meat uncooked, it changes the taste.

parts.body: Hey I like that changed taste!
parts.job: uk|Hey I like that changed taste!

parts.body: Ugh, look how small and sickly the bison are here.
parts.job: uk|Ugh, look how small and sickly the bison are here.

parts.body: The foreign merchant calls them, "cows..?"
parts.job: uk|The foreign merchant calls them, "cows..?"

parts.prefix: v1;0;Il est beau notre village, tu ne trouve pas? /
parts.body: Our village is beautiful, don't you think?
parts.job: uk|Our village is beautiful, don't you think?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Magnifique! Et on y travaille dur! /
parts.body: Splendid! And we work hard at it!
parts.job: uk|Splendid! And we work hard at it!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Le soleil se lève où, déjà? J'oublie toujours. /
parts.body: Where does the sun rise, again? I keep forgetting.
parts.job: uk|Where does the sun rise, again? I keep forgetting.

parts.body: North, where else?
parts.job: uk|North, where else?

parts.prefix: v1;0;Tu penses que la récolte sera bonne cette année? /
parts.body: Do you think the harvest will be good this year?
parts.job: uk|Do you think the harvest will be good this year?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Qui sait, avec le temps qu'il a fait. /
parts.body: Who knows, with the weather we've had.
parts.job: uk|Who knows, with the weather we've had.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Il n'y a plus de saisons. /
parts.body: Seasons don't make sense here.
parts.job: uk|Seasons don't make sense here.

parts.prefix: v1;0;Tu as entendu parler des Indiens? /
parts.body: Have you heard of those Indian people?
parts.job: uk|Have you heard of those Indian people?

parts.prefix: v2;30;Il paraît qu'ils sont très bizarres. /
parts.body: People say they are very strange.
parts.job: uk|People say they are very strange.

parts.prefix: v1;60;J'ai même entendu dire que leur nourriture brûle! /
parts.body: Apparently their food burns!
parts.job: uk|Apparently their food burns!

parts.body: Like calva?
parts.job: uk|Like calva?

parts.body: No, worse!
parts.job: uk|No, worse!

parts.body: Those Byzantines get on my nerves!
parts.job: uk|Those Byzantines get on my nerves!

parts.prefix: v2;30;Oui, tu as vu comme ils nous prennent de haut? /
parts.body: You saw how high and mighty they get?
parts.job: uk|You saw how high and mighty they get?

parts.prefix: v1;60;Tout ça parce qu'ils prétendent être romains. /
parts.body: All that because they claim to be Romans.
parts.job: uk|All that because they claim to be Romans.

parts.prefix: v2;100;Quelle blague. Des romains dégénérés, alors. /
parts.body: What a joke. Degenerated Romans, then.
parts.job: uk|What a joke. Degenerated Romans, then.

parts.prefix: v1;130;On devrait organiser un raid chez eux. /
parts.body: We should organise a raid on them!
parts.job: uk|We should organise a raid on them!

parts.body: We are Vikings after all!

parts.prefix: v1;60;Sa Majesté Guillaume le Conquérant, Duc de Normandie et Roi d'Angleterre, ignare! /
parts.body: His Majesty William the Conqueror, Duke of Normandy and King of England, you fool!
parts.job: uk|His Majesty William the Conqueror, Duke of Normandy and King of England, you fool!

parts.body: Where is England?
parts.job: uk|Where is England?

parts.prefix: v1;120;De l'autre côté de la mer. Quelle ignorance! /
parts.body: On the other side of the sea. Such ignorance!
parts.job: uk|On the other side of the sea. Such ignorance!

parts.body: Of which sea, my Lord?
parts.job: uk|Of which sea, my Lord?

parts.body: Such insolence! Enough!
parts.job: uk|Such insolence! Enough!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Etre berger est un métier très noble. /
parts.body: Being a shepherd is a noble craft.
parts.job: uk|Being a shepherd is a noble craft.

parts.body: Noble? Shepherd?
parts.job: uk|Noble? Shepherd?

parts.prefix: v1;50;N'avons nous pas été choisis par Dieu pour recevoir la Bonne Nouvelle? /
parts.body: Have we not been chosen by God to hear the Good News?
parts.job: uk|Have we not been chosen by God to hear the Good News?

parts.prefix: v2;90;Ah, oui. Pendant que vous vous occupiez des agneaux nouveau-nés - en Décembre. /
parts.body: Ah, yes. While you were taking care of the newly-born lambs - in December.
parts.job: uk|Ah, yes. While you were taking care of the newly-born lambs - in December.

parts.prefix: v1;130;Et alors? Peut être qu'à Bethléem il n'y a pas de saisons. Comme ici! /
parts.body: And so? Maybe in Bethlehem there are no seasons. Like here!
parts.job: uk|And so? Maybe in Bethlehem there are no seasons. Like here!

parts.prefix: v1;0;La vrai force des normands, c'est leurs outils et leurs armes. /
parts.body: The true strength of the Normans lie in their weapons and tools.
parts.job: uk|The true strength of the Normans lie in their weapons and tools.

parts.body: And hence in their smiths?
parts.job: uk|And hence in their smiths?

parts.body: Indeed!
parts.job: uk|Indeed!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Pourquoi est-ce toujours les femmes qui construisent? /
parts.body: Why are the women always the ones building?
parts.job: uk|Why are the women always the ones building?

parts.prefix: v2;40;Si ça te gène, je m'occupe du prochain bâtiment. /
parts.body: If it bothers you, I'll take care of the next one.
parts.job: uk|If it bothers you, I'll take care of the next one.

parts.prefix: v1;80;Vraiment? Tu es adorable! Alors, pour les rideaux, n'oublie pas de... /
parts.body: Really! That is so sweet! So, regarding the drapes, don't forget to...
parts.job: uk|Really! That is so sweet! So, regarding the drapes, don't forget to...

parts.prefix: v2;120;En fait non, je vais te laisser faire. /
parts.body: Actually no, I think I'll let you do it.
parts.job: uk|Actually no, I think I'll let you do it.

parts.prefix: v1;0;Je suis passé devant l'atelier de l'alchimiste hier. /
parts.body: I walked in front of the alchemist workshop yesterday.
parts.job: uk|I walked in front of the alchemist workshop yesterday.

parts.prefix: v1;40;Il y avait une odeur d'œuf pourris horrible! /
parts.body: There was a smell of rotten eggs!
parts.job: uk|There was a smell of rotten eggs!

parts.prefix: v2;80;Il paraît qu'il essaye de fabriquer la pierre philosophale! /
parts.body: They say he's trying to create the philosopher's stone!
parts.job: uk|They say he's trying to create the philosopher's stone!

parts.prefix: v1;120;Moi j'ai entendu qu'il veut résusciter les morts. /
parts.body: I've heard he wants to resuscitate the dead.
parts.job: uk|I've heard he wants to resuscitate the dead.

parts.prefix: v2;160;Et moi qu'il va fabriquer un monstre avec des cadavres! /
parts.body: And me that he will create a monster from body parts!
parts.job: uk|And me that he will create a monster from body parts!

parts.body: How horrible!
parts.job: uk|How horrible!

parts.prefix: v2;220;C'était un garçon si charmant pourtant... /
parts.body: And he was such a sweet boy...
parts.job: uk|And he was such a sweet boy...

parts.prefix: v1;0;Tu as visité les nouvelles archives? /
parts.body: Have you visited the new archives?
parts.job: uk|Have you visited the new archives?

parts.prefix: v1;30;On y voit ce que tout le monde fait! /
parts.body: You can see what everyone is doing!
parts.job: uk|You can see what everyone is doing!

parts.body: Oh, really... and, euh...
parts.job: uk|Oh, really... and, euh...

parts.body: Yes, I saw your panel.
parts.job: uk|Yes, I saw your panel.

parts.body: You should be ashamed of yourself.
parts.job: uk|You should be ashamed of yourself.

parts.prefix: v1;0;J'adore l'odeur de pain qui sort de la boulangerie. /
parts.body: I love the smell of fresh bread coming out of the bakery.
parts.job: uk|I love the smell of fresh bread coming out of the bakery.

parts.prefix: v2;40;Il ne nous manque plus que quelqu'un sachant faire des croissants. /
parts.body: Now we only need someone who knows how to make croissants.
parts.job: uk|Now we only need someone who knows how to make croissants.

parts.body: Our church is truly magnificent!
parts.job: uk|Our church is truly magnificent!

parts.prefix: v2;30;Elle montre que nous sommes un village pieux. /
parts.body: It shows that we are a pious village.
parts.job: uk|It shows that we are a pious village.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Et elle est plus grande que celle du village voisin! /
parts.body: And it's bigger than that of the village next door!
parts.job: uk|And it's bigger than that of the village next door!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Maintenant que nous avons une auberge, nous allons pouvoir commercer! /
parts.body: Now that we have an inn, we can trade!
parts.job: uk|Now that we have an inn, we can trade!

parts.prefix: v2;40;Autrement dit, les marchands de passage vont se servir dans nos resources. /
parts.body: In other words, merchants passing by will help themselves to our resources.
parts.job: uk|In other words, merchants passing by will help themselves to our resources.

parts.body: You've always been cynical.
parts.job: uk|You've always been cynical.

parts.prefix: v1;0;J'adore le marché! Tellement de marchandises superbes! /
parts.body: I love the market! So many fine goods!
parts.job: uk|I love the market! So many fine goods!

parts.prefix: v2;40;On se sent moins isolé maintenant. /
parts.body: We feel less isolated now it's there.
parts.job: uk|We feel less isolated now it's there.

parts.body: But no richer...
parts.job: uk|But no richer...

parts.prefix: v1;0;La taverne est certainement la meilleure chose qu'on ait construite. /
parts.body: The tavern is surely the best thing we've build in the village.
parts.job: uk|The tavern is surely the best thing we've build in the village.

parts.prefix: v2;40;Personne ici ne dira le contraire! /
parts.body: Nobody here will challenge that!
parts.job: uk|Nobody here will challenge that!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Hahaha! Nous sommes imparables. Nos navires impressionnants et honorables chevaliers sont le fléau du monde!. /
parts.body: Hahaha! We are unstoppable. Our impressive ships and honorable knights are the scourge of the world!
parts.job: uk|Hahaha! We are unstoppable. Our impressive ships and honorable knights are the scourge of the world!

parts.prefix: v2;40;Et quels sont nos ennemis? Un groupe de tricksters romains et amoureux de la pierre Maya /
parts.body: And what are our enemies? A bunch of Roman tricksters and Maya stone lovers?
parts.job: uk|And what are our enemies? A bunch of Roman tricksters and Maya stone lovers?

parts.prefix: v1;80;Ne pas oublier les fous des neiges qui n'ont même pas le concept de l'argent! /
parts.body: Don't forget the snow fools who don't even have the concept of money!
parts.job: uk|Don't forget the snow fools who don't even have the concept of money!

parts.prefix: v2;120;Hahaha! La vie normande est la meilleure du monde! Merveilleux cidre, meilleurs outils. Ah, c'est notre âge d'or! /
parts.body: Hahaha! The Norman life is the best in the world! Wonderful Cider, best tools. Ah, this is our golden age.
parts.job: uk|Hahaha! The Norman life is the best in the world! Wonderful Cider, best tools. Ah, this is our golden age.

parts.prefix: v1;160;Et nous arrivons à le partager! /
parts.body: And we get to share it!
parts.job: uk|And we get to share it!

parts.body: Hahaha!
parts.job: uk|Hahaha!

rows.raw: //* The part before the ";" is the title, after it the description

parts.body: Stranger
parts.job: uk|Stranger

parts.body: We are wary of strangers around here, newcomer. But deal fairly with us and you will find people here hospitable.
parts.translation: Ми обережні з незнайомцями, але поводься гідно і ти побачиш як гостепрімни наші люди.

parts.body: Familiarity
We have seen you around before, and no chickens seem to have gone missing. Continue this and we will get along.
parts.translation: Ми тебе бачили кілька разів і досі не пропало жодної курки. Продовжуй в тому ж дусі і ми, можливо, порозуміємося.

parts.body: Known Face
parts.job: uk|Known Face

parts.body: You seem to have made a good impression on many of us.
parts.job: uk|You seem to have made a good impression on many of us.

parts.body: Regular Visitor
Welcome, $name! It's good to see you again.
parts.job: uk|Welcome, $name! It's good to see you again.

parts.body: Fellow Explorer
parts.job: uk|Fellow Explorer

parts.body: Huh, you seem to also be stranded in this world. Well, we can explore this new place together and make a profit!
parts.job: uk|Huh, you seem to also be stranded in this world. Well, we can explore this new place together and make a profit!

parts.body: Favourite Trader
parts.job: uk|Favourite Trader

parts.body: Ah, $name! All the village was waiting for your return.
parts.job: uk|Ah, $name! All the village was waiting for your return.

parts.body: Friend of the Village
parts.job: uk|Friend of the Village

parts.body: We are not known for trusting people easily, but my good friend $name, you have really shown we can trust you!
parts.job: uk|We are not known for trusting people easily, but my good friend $name, you have really shown we can trust you!

parts.body: Ally
parts.job: uk|Ally

parts.body: In this strange world, everyone needs allies. Consider us one, for all of the help you have given us.
parts.job: uk|In this strange world, everyone needs allies. Consider us one, for all of the help you have given us.

parts.body: One of Us
parts.job: uk|One of Us

parts.body: It's always a pleasure to see you $name. You may come from distant lands, but you are really one of us now.
parts.job: uk|It's always a pleasure to see you $name. You may come from distant lands, but you are really one of us now.

parts.body: Natural Leader
$name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Normans. They will follow you anywhere.
parts.job: uk|$name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Normans. They will follow you anywhere.

parts.body: The Next of Kinniken
parts.job: uk|The Next of Kinniken

parts.body: Nuisance
We are watching you, $name. Be on your guard.
parts.job: uk|We are watching you, $name. Be on your guard.

parts.body: Unpleasant Outsider
You have shown to be a real nuisance around here. Be happy we haven't kicked you out yet.
parts.translation: Ти показав справжнє порушення спокою в нашому поселенні. Будь щасливий, що з тобою ще розмовляють.

parts.body: Public Enemy
parts.job: uk|Public Enemy

parts.body: Your presence here is barely tolerated. One wrong move and you've had it.
parts.translation: Твоя присутність тут нестерпно. Один невірний крок, і ти зрозумієш про що я тлумачу!

parts.prefix: art_merchant.keepstall=Des perles pour des cochons, comme ils disent ici. /
parts.body: Pearls before swines, as they say here.
parts.job: uk|Pearls before swines, as they say here.

parts.prefix: art_merchant.greeting=Aucune ville dans le monde n'est comparable à Constantinople. /
parts.body: No city in the world can compare with Constantinople.

parts.prefix: art_merchant.greeting=Les gens ici sont des barbares. /
parts.body: People here are barbarians.
parts.translation: Жодне місто світу не зрівняється з Константинополем.

parts.prefix: art_merchant.greeting=Nous les byzantins sommes les derniers vrais romans. Admirez notre civilisation! /
parts.body: We Byzantines are the last true Romans. Bask in the glory of our civilisation.
parts.translation: Ми, візантійці, останні справжні римляни. Насолоджуйтесь нашою цивілізацією!

parts.prefix: boy.greeting=Quand je serai grand, je veux être comme papa. /
parts.body: When I grow up, I want to be like dad!
parts.translation: Коли я виросту, я хочу стати таким як мій батько!

parts.body: Let's bring back that golden wheat.
parts.job: uk|Let's bring back that golden wheat.

parts.prefix: farmer.collectcrop=On dirait que le blé est mûr. /
parts.body: Looks like the wheat is ripe.
parts.job: uk|Looks like the wheat is ripe.

parts.body: I sow, and then I will harvest.
parts.job: uk|I sow, and then I will harvest.

parts.prefix: guard.greeting=Vous avez l'air un peu faible, $name. Je vous protègerais si vous avez des ennuis. /
parts.body: You look a bit scrawny, $name. I'll protect you if you get into trouble.
parts.job: uk|You look a bit scrawny, $name. I'll protect you if you get into trouble.

parts.prefix: guildmaster.greeting=Les artisans ne valent rien sans quelqu'un pour les superviser. /
parts.body: Artisans are no good without someone to manage them.
parts.translation: Ремісники не такі хороші, якщо ними не управляють.

parts.prefix: knight.greeting=$name, saviez-vous que j'ai combattu à Hastings? /
parts.body: $name, did you know I fought at Hastings?
parts.job: uk|$name, did you know I fought at Hastings?

parts.prefix: knight.greeting=Je n'obéi qu'au Roi Guillaume, Duc de Normandie, et à Dieu. Dans cet ordre. /
parts.body: I only obey King William, Duke of Normandy, and God. In that order.
parts.translation: $ Name, чи знаєш ти що я воював при Гастінгсі?

parts.prefix: knight.greeting=Je prend possession de cette terre au nom du Duc de Normandie! /
parts.body: I claim this strange land for the Duke of Normandy!
parts.translation: Я оголосив цю чужу землю власністю герцога Нормандії!

parts.body: I rule those lands.

parts.prefix: knight.patrol=La force fait le droit, et je suis fort. /
parts.body: Might is right, and I am mighty.
parts.translation: Могушество во славу справедливості, і я могутнім.

parts.body: Nobody here appreciates art.
parts.job: uk|Nobody here appreciates art.

parts.prefix: lady.maketapestry=Peut-être que ces pièces seront moins glauques avec ces tapisseries. Peut-être. /
parts.body: Maybe this place will look less dingy with those on the walls. Maybe.
parts.job: uk|Maybe this place will look less dingy with those on the walls. Maybe.

parts.prefix: lady.greeting=Ma sœur a épousé un duc. Je vis ici. /
parts.body: My sister married a Duke. I live here.
parts.translation: Моя сестра вийшла заміж за герцога, а я животію тут.

parts.prefix: lady.greeting=Vous auriez dû voir le château de mon père. Ca c'était une vrai forteresse. /
parts.body: You should have seen my father's castle. Now that was an impressive fortress.
parts.translation: Ви повинні побачити замок мого батька. Це досить вражаюча фортеця.

parts.prefix: lumberman.bringbackresourceshome=Même ma femme devra admettre que c’est beaucoup de bois. /
parts.body: Even the wife will have to admit that's a lot of wood.
parts.job: uk|Even the wife will have to admit that's a lot of wood.

parts.body: Watch me cut down that tree!
parts.job: uk|Watch me cut down that tree!

parts.body: Nice sapling over there.
parts.job: uk|Nice sapling over there.

parts.prefix: lumberman.plantsaplings=Bientôt ce sera un arbre magnifique ! Et je le couperais. /
parts.body: Soon this will be a big, majestic tree! And I'll cut it down.
parts.job: uk|Soon this will be a big, majestic tree! And I'll cut it down.

parts.prefix: miner.cooking=Ca c’est de la vrai cuisson. /
parts.body: Now this is serious cooking.
parts.job: uk|Now this is serious cooking.

parts.prefix: miner.mining=Miner est un art, vous savez. /
parts.body: Mining is an art, you know.
parts.job: uk|Mining is an art, you know.

parts.prefix: miner.mining=Personne d’autre dans le village n’a la force et l’endurance nécessaire à ce travail. Et vous pensez qu’ils sont reconnaissants ? /
parts.body: Nobody else in the village has the strength and endurance to do this job. And what thanks do I get?
parts.job: uk|Nobody else in the village has the strength and endurance to do this job. And what thanks do I get?

parts.prefix: monk.greeting=Dieu soit avec toi, mon frère. /
parts.body: God be with you, brother.

parts.prefix: monk.makebooks=Si la vanité n’était pas un péché, je dirai que mes manuscrits sont les plus beaux du pays. /
parts.body: If vanity was not a sin, I would say my manuscripts are the finest in the land.
parts.translation: Якби марнославство не було гріхом, я б тоді сказав що мої манускрипти кращі в цих землях.

parts.prefix: oriental_merchant.keepstall=Venez voir des produits de luxes tels que les gens d’ici ne voient jamais ! /
parts.body: Come and see luxuries the like of which people here only dream about!
parts.job: uk|Come and see luxuries the like of which people here only dream about!

parts.prefix: oriental_merchant.greeting=Ce pays est riche, mais fallait il vraiment qu'il soit si froid? /
parts.body: This land is rich, but does it have to be so cold?
parts.job: uk|This land is rich, but does it have to be so cold?

parts.prefix: oriental_merchant.greeting=Etes vous allez à Cordoue? Ca, c'est une ville civilisée. /
parts.body: Have you been to Cordoba? Now that is a civilised place.
parts.translation: Ви бували на Кордоба? Зараз це досить цивілізоване місце.

parts.prefix: plant_merchant.keepstall=Je vend toutes les herbes dont vous aurez jamais besoin. /
parts.body: I sell all the herbs you'll ever need.
parts.job: uk|I sell all the herbs you'll ever need.

parts.prefix: plant_merchant.greeting=Some people say I'm a dreamer, but I'm not the only one... /
parts.translation: Деякі вважають мене мрійником, але я не один такий ...

parts.prefix: priest.gopray.chosen=Prier est plus dur qu’il n’y paraît. /
parts.body: Praying is more work than it looks.
parts.translation: У молитві більше роботи, ніж виглядає з першого погляду.

parts.body: Blessings on you, my son.

parts.prefix: priest.makeamulets=Ceci ne devrait pas être vu par un étranger… /
parts.body: This should not be seen by outsiders...

parts.prefix: seneschal.greeting=J'ai hâte de retourner à la cours du roi. /
parts.body: I am impatient to go back to the royal court.
parts.translation: Я керую цією землею на славу мого короля.

parts.prefix: seneschal.greeting=Je gère ces terres pour mon roi. /
parts.body: I manage those lands for my king.
parts.translation: Я з нетерпінням чекаю повернення до королівського двору.

parts.prefix: smith.makenormantools=Les outils normands sont les meilleurs du monde. /
parts.body: Norman tools are the finest in the world.
parts.job: uk|Norman tools are the finest in the world.

parts.prefix: smith.makenormanweapons=N'essayez pas d'affronter un homme armé par mes soins. /
parts.body: Don't try fighting a man armed by me.
parts.job: uk|Don't try fighting a man armed by me.

parts.body: Viking magic is powerful magic.
parts.job: uk|Viking magic is powerful magic.

parts.prefix: viking_merchant.keepstall=Venez et achetez. Je ne vous parlerai pas des sacrifices nécessaires pour rendre ces amulettes puissantes. /
parts.body: Come and buy. I won't tell you what sacrifices were made to make those amulets strong.
parts.job: uk|Come and buy. I won't tell you what sacrifices were made to make those amulets strong.

parts.body: Today I come to trade. Tomorrow...
parts.translation: Ця земля - ​​земля вікінгів. Англія - ​​земля вікінгів. Сицилія - ​​земля вікінгів. Ми правимо!

parts.prefix: viking_merchant.greeting=Cette terre appartient aux vikings. L'Angleterre aussi. La Sicile aussi. Vive nous! /
parts.body: This land is viking land. England is viking land. Sicily is viking land. We rule!
parts.translation: Сьогодні я прийшов торгувати. Завтра - як знати ...

parts.prefix: villager.becomeadult=Il est l’heure de devenir quelqu’un ! /
parts.body: Time to become something in the world!
parts.job: uk|Time to become something in the world!

parts.body: I think I'll go play outside.
parts.job: uk|I think I'll go play outside.

parts.prefix: villager.makeboudin=Vous ne le mangeriez pas si vous saviez comment c’est fait. /
parts.body: You wouldn't eat it if you knew how it was made.
parts.job: uk|You wouldn't eat it if you knew how it was made.

parts.prefix: villager.brewpotions=Un jour je serais un maître alchimiste ! /
parts.body: One day I will be a master alchemist!
parts.translation: Одного разу я стану великим алхіміком!

parts.body: To arms! To arms!
To arms, citizens!
Montjoi Saint-Denis!
All for one!

parts.prefix: villager.godrink=C'est à boire qu'il nous faut! /
parts.body: I need a drink!

parts.prefix: villager.godrink=Un cidre n'a jamais fait de mal à personne. /
parts.body: A cider never hurt anyone.

parts.prefix: villager.gopray.chosen=Ca fait longtemps que je n’ai pas prié… /
parts.body: Long time since I last prayed…
parts.translation: Багато часу пройшло з моєї останньої молитви.

parts.prefix: villager.gopray=Je parle à Dieu, pas vous, $name. /
parts.body: I'm speaking to God, not you, $name.
parts.job: uk|I'm speaking to God, not you, $name.

parts.body: I am tired.

parts.prefix: villager.gorest=La vie ici est un peu morne. /
parts.body: Life here is a little dull.
parts.job: uk|Life here is a little dull.

parts.body: Nothing exciting ever happens here.

parts.prefix: villager.gorest=Un peu de repos me ferait du bien... /
parts.body: I could do with some rest...
parts.job: uk|I could do with some rest...

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Après une bonne nuit de sommeil, je suis sur pied! /
parts.body: I got some good sleep last night! I feel refreshed!
parts.job: uk|I got some good sleep last night! I feel refreshed!

parts.body: Beautiful day, isn't it?
parts.job: uk|Beautiful day, isn't it?

parts.body: Hello, $name!
parts.job: uk|Hello, $name!

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Il va pleuvoir, je le sens /
parts.body: It's going to rain, I can feel it.
parts.translation: Я не пам'ятаю Нормандію такої досконалої як зараз.

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Je ne me souvenais pas de la Normandie comme ça. /
parts.body: I didn't remember Normandy quite like that.
parts.job: uk|I didn't remember Normandy quite like that.

parts.prefix: villager.harvestwarts=Heuresement que je porte des gants. /
parts.body: Thank God I'm wearing gloves.

parts.prefix: villager.makeglassbottles=Une fiole de qualité, c'est une potion réussie! /
parts.body: A well-made bottle makes for a successful potion!
parts.translation: Для успішного зельеваренія потрібні добре зроблені бутилькі!

parts.prefix: villager.plantwarts=Seul Maître Vif-argent aurait pu comprendre comment cultiver ces horreurs. /
parts.body: Only Master Vif-argent could have understood how to grow those abominations.
parts.translation: Лише знання Vif-argent дають розуміння, як виростити цю мерзоту.

parts.prefix: weapon_merchant.keepstall=Vous ne voulez pas savoir ce qui est arrivé à l’homme qui m’a fait cette cicatrice. Mais vous pouvez acheter la lame que j’ai utilisée. /
parts.body: You do not want to know what happened to the man who gave me that scar. But you can buy the blade I used.

parts.prefix: weapon_merchant.greeting=Vous voulez vraiment savoir comment j'ai survécu toutes ces années voyageant seul avec des marchandises précieuses? /
parts.body: Do you want to know how I survived all those years travelling alone with valuable merchandise?
parts.translation: Хочеш дізнатися як я виживав всі ці роки, подорожуючи один з дорогими товарами?

parts.prefix: wife.delivergoodshousehold="Vas chercher ci, vas chercher ça", ils me disent. Un jour je refuserais ! /

parts.prefix: wife.gethousethresources=On dirait que mon mari a travaillé pour une fois. /

parts.prefix: wife.getresourcesforbuild=Je part chercher une tonne ou deux de matériaux. Je suis plus forte que j’en ai l’air ! /

parts.prefix: wife.makebread=Mon pain est le meilleur du village. /

parts.prefix: wife.construction=Ca va être un bâtiment superbe. /

parts.prefix: wife.construction=Je construis, je construis, comme seule une femme le peu ! /

parts.prefix: wife.construction=Les hommes n’ont pas la finesse nécessaire au travail de précision. /

parts.translation: Цю буде одне з прекрасних будівель.

parts.prefix: wife.getgoodshousehold=Pourquoi est ce toujours moi qui doit tout aller chercher ? /

parts.job: uk|Why am I always the one sent to pick stuff up?

parts.prefix: wool_merchant.keepstall=Toute la laine rose qu’il vous faut ! /

parts.prefix: wool_merchant.greeting=Les textiles hollandais sont les meilleurs à l'ouest de Cathay. /

parts.translation: Голландська текстиль - кращий на захід від Китаю.

parts.prefix: wife.makecider=Préparer le cidre n’est pas le pire travail par ici. /

parts.prefix: wife.makecalva=Une boisson d'homme, faite par une femme. /

parts.body: I obey to God only.

parts.body: I salute you!

parts.prefix: villager.childobserveconstruction=C'est quand même un peu bizarre que seules les femmes construisent chez nous. /

parts.body: Impressive!

parts.prefix: villager.goonpilgrimage=Que Dieu bénisse cette cathédrale ! Que Dieu bénisse la Normandie ! /

parts.body: I'm lonely, so lonely…

parts.body: The Normans seem a hardy folk, with a hearty cooking and a liking for strong alcohol. When drunk, they speak of their lost homeland on the French coast, wherever that is, and boast of their widespread conquests in mysterious places like "England" or "Sicily".

parts.job: uk|The Abbot is a man of God tasked with keeping the Normans he leads on the straight and narrow.

parts.body: The famous Vif-Argent is a wise man who is known to dabble in potions and alchemy in an attempt to figure out the secrets of this bizarre land.

parts.body: Observation on the World
parts.job: uk|Observation on the World

parts.body: Since the night where the world shook and many Indian villages as well as those of other nations were carried away to this strange world, I have prayed to the Goddess for understanding and wisdom on the nature and purpose of this world. I believe she heard my prayers when she sent to me a young and valiant explorer whose work has been invaluable in gathering the information present in this document. Since reality is an illusion in this world even more than in our old lands, I will refer it henceforth as the "Maya" - the world of dreams.

parts.body: General description of the Maya
parts.job: uk|General description of the Maya

parts.body: As has been widely noted since our transfer to this world, the Maya world seems to be a boundless spread of lands of regular types, without seasons, tall mountains, deep oceans or any great variety. I can further add that if it limitless toward the four cardinal points, we have proven that it extends no further than ninety heights of men towards the sky and thirty deep in the ground. It is clear that it is not similar to the world of our birth, but something made to look like it. It is fertile and seems meant to support the livelihood of men like us.

parts.body: Of the animals and plants to be found in the Maya
parts.job: uk|Of the animals and plants to be found in the Maya

parts.body: Investigations of the various lands to be found in the Maya have shown a remarkable fact: while this world contains but a tiny portion of the plants and animals we knew on the banks of the Ganges, almost all of them are directly useful to our village folks. Even the flowers, present in only two kinds, provide us with precious red and yellow dyes, more vivid than what we knew earlier. The multi-armed creatures that swim alone in the empty oceans themselves provide black dye, and for all their fearsome looks they have never been know to attack. From this I can only conclude that the Maya world has been made at least in part for us humans. Only a God or a Goddess could have created this universe, and I believe that it was done for a benevolent purpose.

parts.body: Of Evil in the Maya
parts.job: uk|Of Evil in the Maya

parts.body: Although I believe this world to be the creation of a benevolent divinity, much that is Evil has also been reported in it. My explorer met many of these creatures, especially when observing this world, and never have they seemed to belong in the Maya. In our lost countries, good and evil was mixed in everything – the tiger that devoured villagers was the same that nursed its cub, the rain that brought us good crop the same that flooded the valley. Here the separation is so stark a child could see it. I must conclude from this that there not one hand but two at work in the Maya – a good one that created those lands, and an other one that populated it with nightmarish creatures. Is the second one a great demon, like the mighty Ravana? I do not know.

parts.body: If I have focused my efforts on describing the Maya instead of explaining it, it is because before my vocation as a sadhu lies my training as a naturalist, who believes that to understand you must first observe. And yet I cannot but conjuncture as to the purpose of all this – this vast new land created for humans, populated with people taken from far away in our former lands. What is our Dharma here? To rebuild our former countries like we remember them? To be truer to ourselves than we were? Are we to fight the evil we see, to clean the land from it? I can do nothing but pray for guidance, and hope that wiser men than me will succeed in unveiling the divine will that took us here.

I can do nothing but pray for guidance, and hope that wiser men than me will succeed in unveiling the divine will that took us here.

parts.body: The Alchemist

My son, it has come to our ears that you seek knowledge beyond what the Lord has seen fit to grant us. Do not fall into heresy! If you need guidance, you should retire to a monastry and pray for it. God smiles on people wise enough to see the limit of their understanding. But you are young and foolish, and I know my advice will fall on deaf ears until you learn the lesson yourself. So have young people always been!<ret><ret>There is another man you can go and see, who might be able to help you, or convince you of the futility of your search. Though he dabbles in things he does not understand, he is educated and clever. Do you wish me to guide you to him?
parts.translation: Син мій, до вух моїх досяг слух, що ти шукаєш знання? Як сказав Господь: стукайте і відкриється вам. Чи не впадай у єресь! Якщо тобі потрібні настанови, ти повинен піти в монастир і помолитися. Бог посміхається людям, які мудрі достатньо, щоб розуміти, як мало вони знають. Але ти молодий і дурний, а мені зрозуміло що мої поради не дійдуть до глухих вух доти поки ти не вивчиш урок самостійно. Такі молодики і завжди такими були! <ret> <ret> Однак, є інший чоловік, до якого ти повинен піти. Він досить МУДО і могутніх, щоб допомогти тобі, або, як мінімум вивчить тебе в марності твоїх пошуків. Незважаючи на те, що він грається з речами, які йому не дано зрозуміти, він вчений і розумний. Чи бажаєш ти, щоб я відправив тебе до нього?

parts.body: His name is Guillaume Vif-argent, and he calls himself an 'alchemist'. I do not have his precise location, but he is known to setup his workshop in the mountains, to best observe the stars.
parts.translation: Ім'я його Guillaume Vif-argent, і кличе він себе 'алхімік'. Я не знаю його точного місцезнаходження, але мені відомо, що майстерня його в горах, щоб краще обдивлятися зірки.

parts.body: You are wiser than you look.
Report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$
parts.job: uk|Report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$

parts.body: Have you found that man? What can you say of him?
parts.job: uk|Have you found that man? What can you say of him?

parts.body: I see his knowledge impresses you. Be wary, $name.
parts.job: uk|I see his knowledge impresses you. Be wary, $name.

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Find the Alchemist's Tower in a mountainous area, then report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$ of $startvillager_villagename$.
parts.job: uk|Find the Alchemist's Tower in a mountainous area, then report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$ of $startvillager_villagename$.

parts.body: The Alchemist

$name, I understand that you have searched throughout the lands for help with discovering the secrets of this world. You should have come to me instead! I have the honour of knowing the greatest mind alive today, the Alchemist Guillaume Vif-argent, whose reputation is second to none amoung those of us that are schooled in philosophy. It is him you should go to.

parts.body: His workshop is setup in mountainous areas, where he studies the rocks and the stars.
parts.translation: Його майстерня побудована в горах, де він вивчає мінерали і зірки.

parts.body: So you will not listen to the most learned man since Plato himself? You disapoint me, $name.
parts.job: uk|So you will not listen to the most learned man since Plato himself? You disapoint me, $name.

parts.body: Report to the Guild Master
What news do you have of the great Alchemist?
parts.translation: Які новини ти приніс від великого алхіміка?

parts.body: I see his mind is as penetrating as always. Listen and learn from him, young $name.
parts.job: uk|I see his mind is as penetrating as always. Listen and learn from him, young $name.

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Find the Alchemist's Tower in a mountainous area, then report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$ of $startvillager_villagename$.
parts.job: uk|Find the Alchemist's Tower in a mountainous area, then report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$ of $startvillager_villagename$.

parts.body: The Alchemist

So you want to know who in our realms would have any knowledge of this world? Not the priests, that is sure. And be wary of the guild masters, they always claim to know far more than they do. There is one man that could help you, maybe - he claimed to be very wise and educated and offered to turn lead into gold for our king back in the old world. I always thought he was shady, but maybe there is something to him.
parts.translation: Отже, ти хочеш дізнатися кому відомі будь-які знання у всіх сферах нашого світу? Це точно не священики. І будь обережний з керуючими гільдіями, вони завжди стверджують що знають більше, ніж є насправді. Але є одна людина, який повинен тобі допомогти, напевно. Він дуже мудрий і вчений і навіть пропонував нашому королю перетворити свинець у золото ще в Старому світі. Я завжди вважав його занадто таємничим, але, напевно, якщо хтось щось і знає, то це він.

parts.body: He has settled in the wilderness, near mountains. He claims he need peace for his work, but I am sure he is hiding something. In any case, his name is Guillaume Vif-argent.
parts.translation: Він проживає на віддалі від поселень, поруч з горами. Він заявляє, що йому потрібен спокій для його досліджень, але мені здається, він просто щось приховує. Так чи інакше, звуть його Guillaume Vif-argent.

parts.body: Probably a wise decision.
Report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$
parts.job: uk|Report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$

parts.body: Have you seen the man?
parts.job: uk|Have you seen the man?

parts.body: So he seems genuine to you? Well, as long as he keeps out of my lord's affairs...
parts.translation: Він здався вам щирі? Ну й добре, головне щоб тримався осторонь від справ мого повелителя ...

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Find the Alchemist's Tower in a mountainous area, then report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$ of $startvillager_villagename$.
parts.job: uk|Find the Alchemist's Tower in a mountainous area, then report to the $startvillager_villagerrole$ of $startvillager_villagename$.

parts.body: A welcome
parts.job: uk|A welcome

parts.body: So you were sent to me to seek knowledge, $name? You were well advised. I am the only real alchemist you will find in this god-forsaken world, my boy. If you wish to learn from me, you will need to help. I can always use more resourceful young men. And should you be motivated by more than pure knowledge, know that while I have not yet succeeded at turning lead into gold, I have managed to turn alchemy into coins at the royal court.
parts.job: uk|So you were sent to me to seek knowledge, $name? You were well advised. I am the only real alchemist you will find in this god-forsaken world, my boy. If you wish to learn from me, you will need to help. I can always use more resourceful young men. And should you be motivated by more than pure knowledge, know that while I have not yet succeeded at turning lead into gold, I have managed to turn alchemy into coins at the royal court.

parts.body: You can settle in the house outside if you wish too. My assistant and me are far too busy to ever retire to it.
parts.translation: Ти можеш поселитися в будинку, що поруч з вежею якщо побажаєш. Мій асистент і я дуже зайняті, щоб там бувати.

parts.body: Then begone with you, I have work to do.
parts.translation: Тоді йди, у мене є робота.

parts.body: Stone collection

I am currently working on analysing the rocks of this world. Cleary they are similar to those of the old one in some ways, but their distribution is different. I need samples now! Or did you think I am the kind of useless philosopher to work from books only?
parts.translation: Моїм поточним проектом є аналіз різних гірських порід цього світу. Вони практично ідентичні породам старого світла, але їх розподіл у світі відрізняється. Мені потрібні зразки! А ти думав я даремний філософ, який може тільки книжки читати?

parts.body: Then why do you bother me?
Good. My assistant will provide you with the tools you need. And rest assured, I do not require you to bring me back diamonds. I have completed my work on those already.
parts.translation: Відмінно. Мій асистент забезпечить тебе необхідним інструментом. І ще, мені не потрібно, щоб ти мені приніс алмази, так як я вже закінчив їх дослідження.

parts.body: Pick up tools

Greetings $name, I'm Master Vif-argent's assistant. Do not be offended by his manners, he is a true man of science, too involved in his work to have time for society! But he is very wise, that I know. Anyway, here are your tools.
parts.job: uk|Greetings $name, I'm Master Vif-argent's assistant. Do not be offended by his manners, he is a true man of science, too involved in his work to have time for society! But he is very wise, that I know. Anyway, here are your tools.

parts.body: Good luck, $name!
parts.job: uk|Good luck, $name!

parts.body: I will have to inform the Master.
Pick up tools from the Alchemist's assistant.
Return with samples
What have you found?
parts.job: uk|What have you found?

parts.body: Good, very good! You are an efficient man, $name. I like that.
parts.job: uk|Good, very good! You are an efficient man, $name. I like that.

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Return with the samples to see the Alchemist.
A burning need

I have big experiences in mind, $name. As you might have observed in your travels this world has no volcanos like those of our old Europe, but the soil is full of lava and it is not uncommon to see streams of it at the surface. I need to know what this lava is made of, and if it can be used to transmute metals. My good Robert is too old for this, but you seem resourceful enough to bring me back the samples I need.
parts.job: uk|I have big experiences in mind, $name. parts.body: Then why do you bother me?
Go and see Robert, he will have the equipment you need.
parts.translation: Сходи до Роберту, у нього є необхідне спорядження.

parts.body: Pick up equipment
parts.job: uk|Pick up equipment

parts.body: It's lava he needs this time? I am sure he will do great work with it! Take those buckets, and good luck. Remember the Master needs all 16 filled.
parts.translation: Тепер йому потрібна лава? Упевнений, він виконав велику роботу з нею! Візьми ці відра і удачі тобі. Пам'ятай, Майстру потрібно заповнити всі 16 відер.

parts.body: Be back soon, $name!
parts.job: uk|Be back soon, $name!

parts.body: I will have to inform the Master.
Pick up equipment from the Alchemist's assistant.
Return with the lava
parts.job: uk|Return with the lava

parts.body: Have you got all of it?
Excellent, this will be most useful for my experiments.
parts.translation: Відмінно, вона буде дуже корисна в моїх експериментах.

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Return with the lava to see the Alchemist.
Explosive needs

Ah, $name! Has the Master given you any urgent task? No? Good, good... I am in trouble, $name. The Master had requested large amounts of that mysterious explosive substance that villagers sometimes find around the villages, but I have been unable to secure enough. He will be bitterly disapointed! Would you be able to help? I'll provide any tools you might require.
parts.job: uk|Ah, $name! Has the Master given you any urgent task? No? Good, good... I am in trouble, $name. The Master had requested large amounts of that mysterious explosive substance that villagers sometimes find around the villages, but I have been unable to secure enough. He will be bitterly disapointed! Would you be able to help? I'll provide any tools you might require.

parts.body: What will I do then?
Thank you! Of course I can provide a bow with arrows if you need those.
parts.translation: Спасибі тобі! Звичайно, я надам тобі лук і стріли.

parts.body: Bring back the gunpowder
parts.job: uk|Bring back the gunpowder

parts.body: Have you been able to find any?
parts.job: uk|Have you been able to find any?

parts.body: How did you manage to get so much so fast? You are really an extraordinary man, $name. I cannot thank you enough for your help!
parts.job: uk|How did you manage to get so much so fast? You are really an extraordinary man, $name. I cannot thank you enough for your help!

parts.body: I will have to inform the Master.
Collect gunpowder for the Alchemist' assistant.
The Great Dig
parts.job: uk|The Great Dig

parts.body: I have been studying the geology of this world, with all the rigour of alchemy. Much of it is strange, but nothing is stranger than the layer of hard rock that my assistant has been unable to break. Maybe he is not as hard-working as he should be, or maybe there is something very interesting underneath, which we are not meant to access. Whichever it is, I intend to change it.<ret><ret>Are you ready for some serious work, $name?
parts.job: uk|I have been studying the geology of this world, with all the rigour of alchemy. Much of it is strange, but nothing is stranger than the layer of hard rock that my assistant has been unable to break. Maybe he is not as hard-working as he should be, or maybe there is something very interesting underneath, which we are not meant to access. Whichever it is, I intend to change it.<ret><ret>Are you ready for some serious work, $name?

parts.body: Then why do you bother me?

Before we can seriously attempt to break this barrier, we are going to need a proper pathway to it. $name, I need you to create a borehole to the bottom of the world. Dig anywhere you want, but I need at least a five metres by five metres square of that "bedrock" exposed to the sun.<ret><ret>Do not worry, you will not have to dig by hand. Go and see my assistant and he will provide you with the best tools alchemy can give.

Go and see my assistant and he will provide you with the best tools alchemy can give.

parts.body: Pick up explosives

So he is really going ahead with his borehole plan? Such a great man, with such ambitions! Of course, now it is up to us to do the actual work. Well, up to you really.<ret><ret>Anyway... Thanks to your powder collection, I have prepared those explosives on his instructions. They should help you dig fast.
parts.translation: Тобто він дійсно планує зробити цю свердловину? Велика людина, з не менш великими амбіціями! Звичайно, тепер справа за нами, зробити реальну роботу. Точніше, справа за тобою. <ret> <ret> У кожному разі ... Спасибі за збір пороху. Я саме приготував цю вибухівку за його рецептом. Вона повинна допомогти тобі швидко ... кхм ... копати.

parts.body: Be careful, and good luck!
I will have to inform the Master.
Pick up explosives from the Alchemist's assistant.
Report to the alchemist
I trust my explosives allowed you to complete this task successfully.
parts.translation: Я впевнений, моя вибухівка дозволить тобі виконати цю задати.

parts.body: Excellent work! You have all the making of a fine alchemist, $name. Performing a task like this without blowing yourself up is a show of skills.<ret><ret>I owe you a lot, $name. Please accept in thanks this alchemical amulet of my invention - your samples were vital in enabling me to complete its design. It will glow when you are close to precious minerals.<ret><ret>I am finalising the plans for breaking through those rocks. Rest a little and come back to see me.
parts.job: uk|Excellent work! You have all the making of a fine alchemist, $name. Performing a task like this without blowing yourself up is a show of skills.<ret><ret>I owe you a lot, $name. Please accept in thanks this alchemical amulet of my invention - your samples were vital in enabling me to complete its design. It will glow when you are close to precious minerals.<ret><ret>I am finalising the plans for breaking through those rocks. Rest a little and come back to see me.

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Dig a 5x5 borehole to the bedrock, then report to the Alchemist.
parts.translation: Викопати свердловину 5x5 до корінної породи, потім повинен алхімікові.

parts.body: Explosive matters

The great day has come, $name! I have been studying how to best concentrate explosive power in order to break through the bedrock, and I believe I have found. A good layer of obsidian should be enough to concentrate the explosion toward the ground and ensure our success. Are you ready?
parts.job: uk|The great day has come, $name! I have been studying how to best concentrate explosive power in order to break through the bedrock, and I believe I have found. A good layer of obsidian should be enough to concentrate the explosion toward the ground and ensure our success. Are you ready?

parts.body: Then why do you bother me?

Robert will give you the explosives. Make sure you install it at the bottom of the borehole and place obsidian blocks on top of the explosives. According to my calculations, you will need at least twenty explosives for the effect to be felt. Don't break your legs on the way down.
parts.translation: Роберт дасть тобі ще вибухівки. Переконайся, що ти встановив її на дно свердловини і уклав шар обсидіану поверх вибухівки. Згідно з моїми розрахунками тобі знадобиться не менше 20 вибухівки, щоб домогтися успіху в нашому починанні.

parts.body: Pick up explosives
I have everything ready for you! Explosives, obsidian and enough wire to be safely away when everything is lit.
parts.translation: У мене вже все готово! Вибухівка, обсидіан і достатня кількість дроту щоб бути достатньо в безпечному віддаленні при детонації.

parts.body: I envy you, my young friend - you will be the first to see the riches hidden below!
parts.translation: Я тобі заздрю, мій юнний друг - ти будеш першим, хто побачить багатства приховані внизу!

parts.body: I will have to inform the Master.
Pick up explosives from the Alchemist's assistant.
parts.translation: Взяти ще вибухівки у асистента алхіміка.

parts.body: Report to the alchemist
So, $name! Did everything work? What great things have you seen below?
parts.job: uk|So, $name! Did everything work? What great things have you seen below?

parts.body: Nothing? Nothing? How can it be? How can anything resists such a concentrated blast? It's impossible, you must have done it wrong! Inept!<ret><ret>Alright, alright, I apologise, $name. Your work has always been spotless. I was naïve to think something as simple as ordinary explosives would work. You will have to leave me to study this carefully. There must be a solution - and think of how valuable must be whatever is underneath, to be protected so well!
parts.job: uk|Nothing? Nothing? How can it be? How can anything resists such a concentrated blast? It's impossible, you must have done it wrong! Inept!<ret><ret>Alright, alright, I apologise, $name. Your work has always been spotless. I was naïve to think something as simple as ordinary explosives would work. You will have to leave me to study this carefully. There must be a solution - and think of how valuable must be whatever is underneath, to be protected so well!

parts.body: I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.
parts.job: uk|I will stay here and pray you change your mind, $name.

parts.body: Place twenty TNT blocks at the bottom of the borehole, cover them with a layer of obsidian and lit them. Report the results to the Alchemist.
parts.translation: Розташувати 20 блоків вибухівки на дні свердловини, покрити шаром обсидіану і активувати. Доповісти про результат алхімікові.

parts.body: The Anomaly

Our failure has been weighing on me, $name. I have thought hard about it since then, and I believe my error was not to concentrate enough on the material itself. Before being an obstacle, it is a mystery of its own. And I have made significant progress, $name! I have managed to craft a powder that reacts to the presence of nearby "bedrock" and I have sent my assistant to use it around here to study the layer from the surface. On the whole, the results confirm my initial impression - it is about constant, sixty metres below sea level.<ret><ret>However... He has found at least one place where it is not the case. The bedrock is closer to the surface there, and seemingly in greater quantities! Will you investigate for me?

parts.body: Then why do you bother me?
Be careful, $name! I do not know what this means, and it might be dangerous.

parts.body: Report to the Alchemist
So you made it back? What did you find?
parts.job: uk|So you made it back? What did you find?

parts.body: A room? Artificial and made out of bedrock? This is the greatest discovery since we arrived in this world... It is the first absolute proof that there are or were people in this world with greater powers than our own. It is nothing like those structures I have heard about, those mines and underground fortresses, impressive constructions but not beyond our reach. This is something else altogether. And you say they had devised for spawning those monsters as well?<ret><ret>$name, I will need to think on this for some time, this is beyond my knowledge and experience. I will also see what we can do to pursue our investigation, as the place you visited was empty, well except for the monsters.

parts.body: Explore the anomaly and report to the Alchemist
A Second Blip
parts.job: uk|A Second Blip

parts.body: $name, I have fantastic news! Robert has found a new anomaly not far from here, and it seems like it is much larger than the first one. Who knows what you will find there? Let me collect myself and we will see what to do. Rest as well; I do not doubt your skills as a warrior will be needed again.

parts.body: When we reached the pyramid, the King took me down to a room deep below. In the middle of it was an obsidian pool filled with lava. He was already half-demented at this stage and rambled as to how he would make his most sacrifices there, throwing in the pool the leaders of every village that opposed him. I do not believe his feverish rants meant much, but I do wonder what purpose that pool had. And where does the lava come from? You should find out.

parts.body: Warrior's Sacrifices
parts.job: uk|Warrior's Sacrifices

parts.body: I was hesitant to speak of it with you, $name, but after your fight in the underground chamber you have more than earned the right to share my knowledge. If King Ixtab spared me when I opposed him, it is because he needed my skills in communicating with the Gods. Since I first arrived in this new world, I have made many sacrifices and often drunk the holy Cacauhaa, and I obtained from the Gods that they help the King’s warriors by binding spells to their arms and armours. The Gods demand much blood in return for powerful enchantments, but the weapons obtained are formidable. The King wanted to keep those rituals for the sole use of his warriors – but I can no longer risk a single man having access to such powerful weapons. Go and see a shaman for me and share those rituals with him.

parts.body: Is it finally over, brave $name ?

parts.body: A door, like the one you had found, but made of indestructible matter and... broken.  It must open in the universe from which the one behind all this comes! But how can we follow him? An ocean of sacrifices would not grant us such favour from the gods.  $name, I fear that your efforts will end here.  For the moment, anyway.<ret><ret>But do not think it was in vain! The human money and weapons you found at the bottom shows the demon was about to use King Ixtab to launch a war in those lands.  And that he left them behind shows that he fled hurriedly at your approach! You might not have defeated him, but you forced it to withdraw. Few men can boast of having done that to a demon.  I salute you, $name.<ret><ret>And I think it is fair that I hand this over to you; I found it in the pyramid in your absence: the crown I had made for King Ixtab.  No one other than you is worthy of it now.  Wear it hence, and it will protect you and allow you to swim underwater like the caiman. Use it well. And know also that the man who possesses it will be recognised throughout Maya lands as King.  If you wish to build your own city, the Mayans will follow you. Farewell, $name.

parts.body: $name, have you heard the inspiring news? A great architect from the lands of the Eastern Franks, the renowned Nicolas de Weilbourg, has been touring nearby villages to raise support for the construction of a great cathedral, a monument to our faith in this new and alien land! While not a Norman, he has learned much of our architecture ever since reaching Normandy in search of work worthy of his talents.<ret><ret>Nearby lords and me have been debating where this marvel should be built - they cannot seem to recognise that $startvillager_villagename$ is the only place worthy of such a monument.
