parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.ChopTrees=Échete anarotitheí poté giatí ta temachisména déntra ftánoun edó, $name? Eínai polý períergo. Ó, ti ki an káno, pántote epipléoun kai prépei na spáso to déntro pros ta páno lígo sigá, eínai énas tétoios pónos.! /
parts.body: Have you ever wondered why chopped down trees float here, $name? It's very strange. No matter what I do, they always float and I have to break the tree upward bit by bit, it's such a pain.
parts.job: ru|Have you ever wondered why chopped down trees float here, $name? It's very strange. No matter what I do, they always float and I have to break the tree upward bit by bit, it's such a pain.

parts.body: Hey $name! Don't take that!
parts.job: ru|Hey $name! Don't take that!

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Ta déntra megálosan kalá aftí ti forá, tósa pollá koútsoura kai fytá. /
parts.body: The trees grew well this time, so many logs and saplings.
parts.job: ru|The trees grew well this time, so many logs and saplings.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Elpízo óti to chorió tha chreiasteí óla aftá ta koútsoura. /
parts.body: I hope the village needs all of these logs.
parts.job: ru|I hope the village needs all of these logs.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Aftó ítan éna megálo déntro! Tóra to chorió boreí na chrisimopoiísei ta koútsourá tou. /
parts.body: That was one big tree! Now the village can use its logs.
parts.job: ru|That was one big tree! Now the village can use its logs.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.GatherGoods=Koitáxte óla aftá ta néa kormoús kai ta fytá pou píra apó tin kopí ton déntron! /
parts.body: Look at all of these new logs and saplings I got from chopping down the trees!
parts.job: ru|Look at all of these new logs and saplings I got from chopping down the trees!

parts.body: Nice sapling over there.
parts.job: ru|Nice sapling over there.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Aftá ta fytá eínai tóso mikrá, merikés forés den boró na pistépso óti tha gínoun tóso megála. /
parts.body: These saplings are so small, sometimes I can't believe that they will become so big.
parts.job: ru|These saplings are so small, sometimes I can't believe that they will become so big.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Eísai tóso charitoméno mikrófyllo, schedón me afínei na xecháso óti tha se kópso ótan megalóseis. /
parts.body: You're so cute little sapling, almost lets me forget I'm going to chop you down when you grow up.
parts.job: ru|You're so cute little sapling, almost lets me forget I'm going to chop you down when you grow up.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=$name, thélete na fytépsete éna fytó? /
parts.body: $name, do you want to plant a sapling?
parts.job: ru|$name, do you want to plant a sapling?

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Ta déntra megalónoun tóso grígora edó, se líges méres gyrízoun apó aftó to mikroskopikó déntro méchri na eínai éna gemáto déntro. /
parts.body: Trees grow so fast here, in a few days they turn from this tiny sapling to being a full tree.
parts.job: ru|Trees grow so fast here, in a few days they turn from this tiny sapling to being a full tree.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=I fýtefsi eínai i efkolóteri douleiá, to móno pou prépei na káno eínai na ta topothetíso sto édafos. /
parts.body: Planting is the easiest job, all I have to do is place them on the ground.
parts.job: ru|Planting is the easiest job, all I have to do is place them on the ground.

parts.prefix: lumberman_byzantine.PlantSaplings=Syntoma tha ginei ena megalo, panemorfo dentro! Kai tha to kopsw.  /
parts.body: Soon this will be a big, majestic tree! And I'll cut it down.
parts.job: ru|Soon this will be a big, majestic tree! And I'll cut it down.

parts.prefix: merchant_art.greeting=Kamía póli ston kósmo den boreí na synkritheí me tin omorfiá kai ti dýnami tis Konstantinoúpolis. /
parts.body: No city in the world can compare with the beauty and might of Constantinople.
parts.translation: Ни один город в мире не может сравниться с Константинополем.

parts.body: We are the last true Romans!
parts.translation: Мы - Византийцы, последние из истинных Римлян.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=I douleiá mou eínai na spáso ta vráchia kai na metatrépso aftá ta vráchia pros epexergasía, aftó eínai. /
parts.body: My job is to break rocks and take those rocks to be smelted, that's it.
parts.job: ru|My job is to break rocks and take those rocks to be smelted, that's it.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=To chéri mou ponáei apó ti chrísi aftís tis pikkáx káthe méra. /
parts.body: My arm hurts from using this pickaxe every day.
parts.job: ru|My arm hurts from using this pickaxe every day.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Éna blok, dýo blok, tría blok, téssera blok, den teleiónei poté. Akrivós to ídio prágma xaná kai xaná. /
parts.body: One block, two block, three block, four block, it never ends. Just the same thing over and over again.
parts.job: ru|One block, two block, three block, four block, it never ends. Just the same thing over and over again.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Éna blok, dýo blok, treis anamonís, eínai aftós o chrysós? Aftó eínai? Vríka to chrysó! CHRYSOS! CHRYSOS! Eímai ploúsios! HAHA-ítan aplá sidírou pou antanaklá se kakó fos. Epistrofí sto exóryxi sidírou kai ánthraka ... /
parts.body: One block, two block, three-wait, is that gold?  That is? I FOUND GOLD! GOLD! GOLD! I'm rich! HAHA-oh, it was just iron reflecting in a bad light. Back to mining iron and coal...
parts.job: ru|One block, two block, three-wait, is that gold?  That is? I FOUND GOLD! GOLD! GOLD! I'm rich! HAHA-oh, it was just iron reflecting in a bad light. Back to mining iron and coal...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Ogdónta blok, ogdónta éna blok, októ dýo blok, ogdónta tría blok ... /
parts.body: Eighty block, eighty one block, eight two block, eighty three block...
parts.job: ru|Eighty block, eighty one block, eight two block, eighty three block...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Geia sou! Pós metaféroun tósa pollá blok kai i dikí mou tóso grígora? Chreiázontai óres gia na káno aftó pou káneis se mia méra. /
parts.body: Hey! How do you carry so many blocks and mine so fast? It takes me hours to do what you do in a day.
parts.job: ru|Hey! How do you carry so many blocks and mine so fast? It takes me hours to do what you do in a day.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=*ghouch* *Ghouch*, misó na ergázomai me ánthraka. /
parts.body: *Cough* *Cough*, I hate working with coal.
parts.job: ru|*Cough* *Cough*, I hate working with coal.

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Gia na kaneis aythn thn douleia h dynamh kai h antoxh einai aparaithta. Kaneis omws den to katalabainei... /
parts.body: In this job strength and endurance is needed. But nobody here notices...
parts.job: ru|In this job strength and endurance is needed. But nobody here notices...

parts.prefix: miner_byzantine.Mining=Eimai perifanos pou eimai Romaios katoikos kai pou douleyw gia thn aytokratoria , an kai einai dyskolh douleia. /
parts.body: I'm proud to be a Roman Citizen working for the glorious Empire, even in this hard job.
parts.job: ru|I'm proud to be a Roman Citizen working for the glorious Empire, even in this hard job.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.makebooks=Ta biblia mou einai merika apo ta kalytera xeirografa ekei exo. /
parts.body: My books are some of the best manuscripts out there.
parts.translation: Мои книги являются одними из лучших рукописей за пределами Византии.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=Giatí o Theós me ékane énan apó tous pio polýtimous ypirétes tou? /
parts.body: Why did God make me one of his most treasured servants?
parts.job: ru|Why did God make me one of his most treasured servants?

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=Os Patriárchis, prépei na odigíso tin prosefchí. /
parts.body: As the Patriarch, I must lead the prayer.
parts.job: ru|As the Patriarch, I must lead the prayer.

parts.body: I understand the troubles He has.
parts.job: ru|I understand the troubles He has.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=Katanoeí ta provlímata pou échoun oi patriárches. /
parts.body: He understands the troubles patriarchs have.
parts.job: ru|He understands the troubles patriarchs have.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gopray=To chorió mou chreiázetai apantíseis apó to Theó! /
parts.body: My village needs answers from God!
parts.job: ru|My village needs answers from God!

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gorest=Óloi chreiázontai ýpno, eidiká ótan eíste igétis enós chorioú. /
parts.body: Everyone needs sleep, especially when you are a leader of a village.
parts.job: ru|Everyone needs sleep, especially when you are a leader of a village.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.gorest=*Chasmouritó* Den boró na odigíso tous iereís ótan eímai kourasménos./
parts.body: *Yawn* I cannot lead priests when I am tired.
parts.job: ru|*Yawn* I cannot lead priests when I am tired.

parts.prefix: patriarch_byzantine.inspectconstruction=I omorfiá vlépei to chorió sas na plisiázei perissótero sto Theó. /
parts.body: Beauty is watching your village get closer to God.
parts.job: ru|Beauty is watching your village get closer to God.

parts.prefix: pastor_byzantine.makebooks=Ta biblia mou einai merika apo ta kalytera xeirografa ekei exo. /
parts.body: My books are some of the best manuscripts out there.
parts.translation: Мои книги являются одними из лучших рукописей за пределами Византии.

rows.raw: //smith_byzantine.MakeIndianTools=Ta romaïkós ergaleia einai ta kalytera ston kosmo. / Roman tools are the best in world.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=Énas kalós sideras prépei na proséfchetai káthe forá kai lígo. /
parts.body: A good smith needs to pray every once and a while.
parts.job: ru|A good smith needs to pray every once and a while.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=Giatí o Theós me ékane éna sídera? /
parts.body: Why did God make me a smith?
parts.job: ru|Why did God make me a smith?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=I prosefchí eínai éna simantikó méros tis romaïkís cheirotechnías. /
parts.body: Praying is an important part of Roman crafting.
parts.job: ru|Praying is an important part of Roman crafting.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gopray=Katanoeí ta provlímata pou échoun oi siderades. /
parts.body: He understands the troubles smiths have.
parts.job: ru|He understands the troubles smiths have.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gorest=Ávrio tha káno pio ómorfa prágmata! /
parts.body: Tomorrow I will craft more beautiful things!
parts.job: ru|Tomorrow I will craft more beautiful things!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gorest=Écho kánei me ktírio gia tin iméra. /
parts.body: I am done with crafting for the day.
parts.job: ru|I am done with crafting for the day.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gorest=Ísos tha oneireftó na káno ta kalýtera ergaleía ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Maybe I will dream of crafting the world's best tools!
parts.job: ru|Maybe I will dream of crafting the world's best tools!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gosocialise=Tha zitíso na do an kápoios chreiázetai na kataskeváso káti. /
parts.body: I will ask to see if anyone needs me to craft something.
parts.job: ru|I will ask to see if anyone needs me to craft something.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.gosocialise=Elpízo óti to chorió ektimá ta ergaleía mou. /
parts.body: I hope that the village appreciates my tools.
parts.job: ru|I hope that the village appreciates my tools.

parts.body: Enough crafting! I need some wine!
parts.job: ru|Enough crafting! I need some wine!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.goDrink=Chreiázomai éna potó gia na me empnéfsei! /
parts.body: I need a drink to inspire me!
parts.job: ru|I need a drink to inspire me!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.goDrink=Káthe kalós siderás chreiázetai éna potó sto télos tis iméras. /
parts.body: Every good blacksmith needs a drink at the end of the day.
parts.job: ru|Every good blacksmith needs a drink at the end of the day.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.goDrink=I cheirotechnía me kánei na dipsá gia to krasí. /
parts.body: Crafting makes me thirsty for wine.
parts.job: ru|Crafting makes me thirsty for wine.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelaxe=Den boreíte na kópsete ta déntra chorís tsekoúri! /
parts.body: You cannot chop down trees without an axe!
parts.job: ru|You cannot chop down trees without an axe!

parts.body: I craft amazing axes.
parts.job: ru|I craft amazing axes.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelaxe=Oi romaïkoí áxones eínai merikoí apó tous kalýterous ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman axes are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: ru|Roman axes are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelaxe=Oi xylourgoí chreiázontai na kánoume tous áxonés tous. /
parts.body: The lumbermen need us to craft their axes.
parts.job: ru|The lumbermen need us to craft their axes.

parts.body: How do you craft your axes $name?
parts.job: ru|How do you craft your axes $name?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Den boreíte na ekmetallefteíte chorís ergaleía kalliérgeias! /
parts.body: You cannot farm without farming tools!
parts.job: ru|You cannot farm without farming tools!

parts.body: I craft amazing farming tools.
parts.job: ru|I craft amazing farming tools.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Romaïká ergaleía kalliérgeias eínai meriká apó ta kalýtera ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman farming tools are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: ru|Roman farming tools are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Oi agrótes chreiázontai na kataskevásoume ta ergaleía tous. /
parts.body: The farmers need us to craft their tools.
parts.job: ru|The farmers need us to craft their tools.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelhoe=Pós dimiourgeíte ta georgiká sas ergaleía $name? /
parts.body: How do you craft your farming tools $name?
parts.job: ru|How do you craft your farming tools $name?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelpickaxe=Den boreíte na to dikí sas chorís pickaxe! /
parts.body: You cannot mine without a pickaxe!
parts.job: ru|You cannot mine without a pickaxe!

parts.body: I craft strong pickaxes.
parts.job: ru|I craft strong pickaxes.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelpickaxe=Ta romaïká pickaxes eínai meriká apó ta kalýtera ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman pickaxes are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: ru|Roman pickaxes are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelpickaxe=Oi anthrakorýchoi mas chreiázontai na kataskevásoume ta pickaxes tous. /
parts.body: The miners need us to craft their pickaxes.
parts.job: ru|The miners need us to craft their pickaxes.

parts.body: How do you craft your pickaxes $name?
parts.job: ru|How do you craft your pickaxes $name?

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelshovel=Den boreíte na chtísete í na skápsete chorís éna ftyári! /
parts.body: You cannot build or dig without a shovel!
parts.job: ru|You cannot build or dig without a shovel!

parts.body: I craft durable shovels.
parts.job: ru|I craft durable shovels.

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelshovel=Romaïká ftyária eínai meriká apó ta kalýtera ston kósmo! /
parts.body: Roman shovels are some of the best in the world!
parts.job: ru|Roman shovels are some of the best in the world!

parts.prefix: smith_byzantine.makesteelshovel=Oi architéktones chreiázontai na kataskevásoume ta ftyária tous. /
parts.body: The architects need us to craft their shovels.
parts.job: ru|The architects need us to craft their shovels.

parts.body: How do you craft your shovels $name?
parts.job: ru|How do you craft your shovels $name?

parts.body: Hello, $name!
Beautiful day, isn't it?
It will rain soon.

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Kamia polh ston kosmo den sygrinete me tin Konstantinoúpoli./
parts.body: No city in the world can compare with Constantinople.
parts.translation: Нет такого города в мире, что мог бы сравниться с Константинополем.

parts.body: We aren't Greek, we're Roman.
We are the last true Romans.

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Varéli sti dóxa tou politismoú mas katá ti diárkeia tis paramonís sas edó. /
parts.body: Bask in the glory of our civilization during your stay here.
parts.job: ru|Bask in the glory of our civilization during your stay here.

parts.body: Welcome to the village, $name!
Look! There's $name!
parts.job: ru|Look! There's $name!

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Eimaste oi Byzantinoi, oi teleutaioi alhthinoi Romaioi. Ypoklitheite stin doxa tou politismou mas. /
parts.body: We are the last true Romans. Bath in the light of our civilisation.
parts.job: ru|We are the last true Romans. Bath in the light of our civilisation.

parts.body: Finally, I have become a Roman citizen!
parts.job: ru|Finally, I have become a Roman citizen!

parts.prefix: villager.huntmonster=Prépei na skotóso aftón ton bárbaro! /
parts.body: I need to kill this barbarian!
I think I'll go play outside.
parts.job: ru|I think I'll go play outside.

parts.body: I will go play now.
parts.job: ru|I will go play now.

parts.prefix: villager.goPlay=$name! Théleis na paíxeis mazí mou? /
parts.body: $name! Do you want to play with me?
parts.job: ru|$name! Do you want to play with me?

parts.body: I want to run!
parts.job: ru|I want to run!

parts.body: The Roman Empire is attacked! To arms!
parts.translation: Римская Империя под атакой! К оружию!

parts.body: The barbarians are here! Defend our village at all costs!
parts.translation: Здесь варвары! Защитите деревню любой ценой!

parts.prefix: villager.childeatgrapes=Orkízomai óti aftá ta stafýlia épesan mónoi tous! /
parts.body: I swear these grapes fell on their own!
parts.translation: Клянусь, этот виноград уже так и лежал здесь!

parts.prefix: villager.childobservevines=Oi enílikes prépei na stamatísoun na chánoun nóstima stafýlia kánontas aftó to apaísio krasí apó aftó! /
parts.body: Adults should stop wasting tasty grapes by making that awful wine from it!
parts.translation: Взрослые должны научиться ценить этот сладкий виноград, а не делать из него это гадкое вино!

parts.prefix: villager.childobserveconstruction=Mia méra tha episkefthó tin Konstantinoúpoli kai tha doúme ti moiázoun me ta pragmatiká romaïká ktíria! /
parts.body: One day I will visit Constantinople and see what real Roman buildings look like!
parts.job: ru|One day I will visit Constantinople and see what real Roman buildings look like!

parts.prefix: villager.childobserveproducealcohol=Dokímasa éna krasí mia forá, eínai aidiastikó. /
parts.body: I tried wine once, it's disgusting.
parts.translation: Я как-то попробовал вино, мне не понравилось.

parts.prefix: villager.gorest=An den koimithó, boreí na symvoún atychímata. /
parts.body: If I do not sleep, accidents can happen.

parts.prefix: villager.gorest=Eímai kourasménos. Páo spíti gia na koimithó. /
parts.body: I'm tired. I'm going home to sleep.

parts.prefix: villager.gorest=Mallon oti tha pao gia ypno. /
parts.body: I think I'm off to go to sleep.
The bread already smells good...
parts.job: ru|The bread already smells good...

parts.body: I am guided by the Holy Father.
parts.job: ru|I am guided by the Holy Father.

parts.body: Oh Lord you skyborn, and mercyful.
parts.job: ru|Oh Lord you skyborn, and mercyful.

parts.prefix: villager.gopray=O paides eulogitai, oi iereis animneite! /
parts.body: The men worship, the clerics chant!
parts.job: ru|The men worship, the clerics chant!

parts.body: Hail virgin nymf!
parts.job: ru|Hail virgin nymf!

parts.body: Oh holy Marry, Great victorius commander!
parts.job: ru|Oh holy Marry, Great victorius commander!

parts.body: You who save me from the bad I thank you...
parts.job: ru|You who save me from the bad I thank you...

parts.prefix: villager.gopray=Laos uperipsoute, eis pantas tous aiones /
parts.body: The people will pray for you, to the never ending eons, amen.
parts.job: ru|The people will pray for you, to the never ending eons, amen.

parts.prefix: villager.goDrink=Óra na ftiáxete éna frésko romaïkó krasí! /
parts.body: Time to get some fresh Roman wine!
parts.job: ru|Time to get some fresh Roman wine!

parts.body: I need a drink.
parts.job: ru|I need a drink.

parts.prefix: villager.goDrink=O oínos tha plýnei ta provlímatá mou. /
parts.body: Wine will wash my troubles away.
parts.job: ru|Wine will wash my troubles away.

parts.prefix: villager.goDrink=Xérate óti to romaïkó krasí eínai to kalýtero ston kósmo? /
parts.body: Did you know that Roman wine is the best in the world?
parts.job: ru|Did you know that Roman wine is the best in the world?

parts.prefix: villager.goDrink=Échei perásei polýs kairós apó tóte pou écho éna potó. /
parts.body: It's been a long time since I have had a drink.
parts.job: ru|It's been a long time since I have had a drink.

parts.prefix: wife_byzantine.DeliverGoodsHousehold=Pragmata opws auto einai ta mona pou mporw na kanw. /
parts.body: Things like this are the only things I can do here.
parts.job: ru|Things like this are the only things I can do here.

parts.prefix: wife_byzantine.GetHouseTHResources=Epitelous o syzygos mou metefere ta agatha opws tou eipa. /
parts.body: My husband has finally delivered his resources like I told him.
parts.job: ru|My husband has finally delivered his resources like I told him.

parts.body: Cooking is really fun.

parts.prefix: wife_byzantine.getGoodsHousehold=Óra na frontízo tin oikogéneiá mou. /
parts.body: Time to take care of my family.
parts.job: ru|Time to take care of my family.

parts.prefix: wife_byzantine.greeting=Tha boroúsa na káno pollá perissótera edó an ímoun ándras, an móno... /
parts.body: I could do so much more here if I was a man, if only...

parts.prefix: wife_byzantine.greeting=To kathikon mas einai na elegxoume tous andres. /
parts.body: Our task is to control our men.
parts.translation: Как и женщины, вы не можете сделать здесь многое

parts.prefix: villager.givespeech=I Romaïkí Aftokratoría eínai megáli kai to chorió mas eínai to Spoudaióteron. /
parts.body: The Roman Empire is great, and our village is the greatest.
parts.job: ru|The Roman Empire is great, and our village is the greatest.

parts.prefix: villager.givespeech=To chorió mas prépei na efcharistísei gia tin igesía tou gia ólo to megaleío tou. /
parts.body: Our village must thank its leadership for all its greatness.
parts.job: ru|Our village must thank its leadership for all its greatness.

parts.prefix: villager.givespeech=Emeís oi Romaíoi échoume tous kalýterous igétes kai tous kalýterous anthrópous. /
parts.body: We Romans have the best leaders and best people.
parts.job: ru|We Romans have the best leaders and best people.

parts.body: He is right!
parts.job: ru|He is right!

parts.body: Glory to us!
parts.job: ru|Glory to us!

parts.body: We can defeat anybody!
parts.job: ru|We can defeat anybody!

parts.prefix: villager.listentospeech=Dóxa ston Theó kai ston Theóchristo igéti! /
parts.body: Glory to God and our Godsend leader!
parts.job: ru|Glory to God and our Godsend leader!

parts.body: Your servitude will be rewarded, $name.
parts.job: ru|Your servitude will be rewarded, $name.

parts.body: Don’t test your luck, child.
parts.job: ru|Don’t test your luck, child.

parts.body: Bow before me...
parts.job: ru|Bow before me...

parts.prefix: oldshepherd_byzantine.greeting=Oi pepoithíseis mou me krátisan kala… /
parts.body: My beliefs kept me going on…
parts.job: ru|My beliefs kept me going on…

parts.prefix: oldshepherd_byzantine.greeting=Voíthisé me na ekpliróso to óneiró mou, $name, kai tha antameiftheíte /
parts.body: Help me fulfil my dream, $name, and you shall be rewarded…
parts.job: ru|Help me fulfil my dream, $name, and you shall be rewarded…

parts.body: For the Boskokrator!

parts.prefix: oldshepherd_byzantine=Ágios Boskokrátor, parakaló evlogíste me kai ta próvatá mou. /
parts.body: Holy Boskokrator, please bless me and my sheep.
parts.translation: Святой Боскократор, благослови меня и моих овец.

parts.prefix: merchant_armour.greeting=Móno ta oraiótera ópla kai ta ópla! /
parts.body: Only the finest armours and weapons!

parts.prefix: merchant_armour.keepStall=Kalós írthate! Sas férno ta kalýtera spathiá pou boreíte na vreíte! /
parts.body: Welcome, welcome! I bring you the best swords you can find!
parts.job: ru|Welcome, welcome! I bring you the best swords you can find!

parts.prefix: merchant_dyes.greeting=Érchomai sta chrómata káthe méra! Periménete, den eímai indós. /
parts.body: I come in colours every day! Wait, I am not Indian.
parts.translation: Я  в цветах каждый день! Подожди, я не индиец.

parts.prefix: merchant_dyes.keepStall=Ela na deis! Vafés apó ólo ton kósmo! /
parts.body: Come and see! Dyes from all around the world!
parts.job: ru|Come and see! Dyes from all around the world!

parts.body: Ti léte gia kápoio nóstimo souvláki, $name? How about some delicious souvlaki, $name?
parts.job: ru|Ti léte gia kápoio nóstimo souvláki, $name? How about some delicious souvlaki, $name?

parts.prefix: merchant_food.keepStall=Óla ta trófima pou thélete na fáte! /
parts.body: All the food you ever want to eat!
parts.job: ru|All the food you ever want to eat!

parts.prefix: merchant_materials.greeting=Eláte na agorásete ta kalýtera oikodomiká yliká! Egó kai i pláti mou tha sas efcharistíso. /
parts.body: Come and buy the finest building materials! Me and my back will thank you.
parts.translation: Подходи и покупай лучшие материалы для строительства. Я и моя спина поблагодарят тебя.

parts.prefix: merchant_materials.keepStall=Ámmos, pétra kai toúvla! Diorite kai chalazía! /
parts.body: Sand, Stone and Bricks! Diorite and Quartz!
parts.job: ru|Sand, Stone and Bricks! Diorite and Quartz!

parts.prefix: merchant_relics.greeting=Pouláo polýtimes cheirotechníes kai ierá koimilia, $name. /
parts.body: I sell valuable crafts and sacred goods, $name.
parts.translation: Я продаю ценные и священные товары, $name.

parts.prefix: merchant_relics.keepStall=Eláte kai deíte tin koryfí tis romaïkís cheirotechnías. /
parts.body: Come, and view the peak of Roman craftsmanship.
parts.job: ru|Come, and view the peak of Roman craftsmanship.

parts.body: Seriously, $name? This skin?

parts.prefix: merchant_textiles.keepStall=Montérna chaliá kai roúcha, ópos akrivós kai stin Konstantinoúpoli! /
parts.body: Trendy carpets and clothes, just like they have in Constantinople!
parts.job: ru|Trendy carpets and clothes, just like they have in Constantinople!

parts.prefix: loneabbot_byzantine.greeting=Kalós ílthate, $name. Boreíte na xekourasteíte apó ta taxídia sas, eíste asfaleís edó. /
parts.body: Welcome, $name. You may rest from your travels, you are safe here.
parts.job: ru|Welcome, $name. You may rest from your travels, you are safe here.

parts.prefix: lonemonk_byzantine.greeting=Den boró na sou prosféro típota, $name /
parts.body: I cannot offer you anything, $name.
parts.job: ru|I cannot offer you anything, $name.

parts.prefix: loneabbot_byzantine.gosocialise=Anypomonó na moirastó tis spoudés mou. /
parts.body: I cannot wait to share my studies.
parts.job: ru|I cannot wait to share my studies.

parts.prefix: lonemonk_byzantine.gosocialise=Anypomonó na moirastó tis spoudés mou. /
parts.body: I cannot wait to share my studies.
parts.job: ru|I cannot wait to share my studies.

parts.prefix: lonemonk_byzantine.plantseeds=Eíthe o Theós na evlogeí aftoús tous spórous. /
parts.body: May God bless these seeds.
parts.job: ru|May God bless these seeds.

parts.prefix: lonemonk_byzantine.collectcrop=Aftés oi kalliérgeies eínai dóro apó ton ídio ton Theó. /
parts.body: These crops are a gift from God himself.
parts.job: ru|These crops are a gift from God himself.

parts.prefix: lonemonk_byzantine.makebread=I megáli thysía ton Yión tha xekinísei me aftó to psomí. /
parts.body: The Son’s great sacrifice will be commenced with this bread.
parts.job: ru|The Son’s great sacrifice will be commenced with this bread.

parts.prefix: villager.plantseeds=Pistévo óti tha échoume ploúsia synkomidí fétos. /
parts.body: I feel that we will have rich harvest this year.
parts.job: ru|I feel that we will have rich harvest this year.

parts.body: I knew it! A rich harvest!
parts.job: ru|I knew it! A rich harvest!

parts.prefix: villager.gostudy=Parakaló, min me apospoún tin prosochí, $name. /
parts.body: Please, do not distract me, $name.
parts.job: ru|Please, do not distract me, $name.

parts.prefix: villager.gotreerelax=Aftó to skieró méros eínai téleio... /
parts.body: This shady place is just perfect…
parts.job: ru|This shady place is just perfect…

parts.prefix: villager.gotreerelax=Tha boroúsa na meíno káto apó aftó to déntro óli tin iméra… /
parts.body: I could stay under this tree all day…
parts.job: ru|I could stay under this tree all day…

parts.prefix: villager.relight=I agápi tou Theoú eínai i móni mou epithymía! /
parts.body: God’s love is my only desire!
parts.job: ru|God’s love is my only desire!

parts.prefix: villager.golookout=Símera, éna ploío tha érthei. To xéro. /
parts.body: Today, a ship will come. I know it.
parts.job: ru|Today, a ship will come. I know it.

parts.prefix: villager.golookout=Mia varetí douleiá, allá touláchiston plirónomai. /
parts.body: A boring job, but at least I get paid.
parts.job: ru|A boring job, but at least I get paid.

parts.body: The Byzantines claim they are the true Romans and are very proud of their characteristic architecture, disciplined military and the masterful icons they craft to worship the Saints. Some say they are a little too proud of their achievements.
parts.translation: Византийцы утверждают, что они настоящие потомки римлян. Они очень гордятся своей характерной архитектурой, дисциплинированными воинами и шедевральными иконами, которые они делают, чтобы восхвалить святых. Говорят, что они немного горделивы.

parts.body: This skilled villager builds beautiful civilized buildings for the village, unlike the nearby desolate shacks built by those barabaric fools.
parts.translation: Этот умелый житель строит  прекрасные цивилизованные здания для деревни. Не то что близлежащие заброшенные лачуги, построенные варварами.

parts.body: The army smith crafts mighty weapons for the village.
parts.translation: Военный кузнец, который делает мощные оружия для деревни.

parts.body: Some argue that the artisan wives are more skillfull than their husbands.
parts.translation: Некоторые утверждают, что жены ремесленников более искусны, чем их мужья.

parts.body: The baron earns his riches off the backs of his subjects, but nevertheless is invaluable in managing the daily needs of the village.
parts.translation: Барон зарабатывает свои богатства трудом своих подданных, но, тем не менее, неоценим в управлении повседневными потребностями деревни.

parts.body: The baroness' duties are way to important to be listed here - thats what she said.
parts.translation: Обязанности баронессы слишком важны, чтобы они могли быть перечисленными здесь - вот что она сказала.

parts.body: This boy will grow up to become a civilized citizen.
parts.translation: Этот мальчик вырастет и станет цивилизованным гражданином.

parts.body: Former leader of a hundred men. He does not want to talk about about the reason for his demotion.
parts.translation: Бывший лидер сотен человек. Он не хочет говорить о причине его понижения в должности.

parts.body: He secures the growth of carrots for the original Imperial bread. And some carrots.
parts.translation: Он защищает производство оригинального имперского хлеба.

parts.body: She makes and markets the original Imperial bread.
parts.translation: Она делает и продаёт оригинальный имперский хлеб.

parts.body: The fisherman fishes for fish, kind of self-explanatory.
This girl will grow up to become a civilized citizen.
parts.translation: Эта девушка вырастет и станет цивилизованным гражданином.

parts.body: The guard sometimes regrets choosing a wife over full training to become a soldier.
parts.translation: Охранник иногда жалеет, что выбрал жену, а не полную подготовку, чтобы стать солдатом.

parts.body: The host is a master in wine making. His wine is the best on this side of the Bosporus.
parts.translation: Хозяин - мастер виноделия. Его вино - лучшее по эту сторону Босфора.

parts.body: The hostesse is a master in food making. Her speciality are the famous souvlakis.
parts.translation: Хозяйка - мастер в приготовлении пищи. Ее специальность - знаменитые саувлаки.

parts.body: She enjoyed great education in Iconography and writing - though she could make more use of that.
parts.translation: Она получила прекрасное образование в области иконографии и письма, хотя могла бы использовать его в большей степени.

parts.body: Lumbermen cut down trees for valuable Imperial wood.
parts.translation: Лесник вырубает деревья для ценных имперских дров.

parts.body: The masons favourite material is diorite - he is even able to turn it into quartz or extravagant mosaics.
parts.translation: Любимым материалом каменщиков является диорит - он даже способен превратить его в кварц или экстравагантную мозаику.

parts.body: This merchant sells weaponry and armoury. The Byzantine armyforge is sure that local made Byzantine tools are superior though.
parts.translation: Этот торговец продает оружие и арсенал. Византийская армия кузница уверена, что местные сделанные византийские инструменты превосходны, хотя...

parts.body: This local merchant secures the flow of goods in his village through clever trade deals with neighbouring settlements.
parts.translation: Этот местный торговец обеспечивает поток товаров в своей деревне через умные торговые сделки с соседними поселениями.

parts.body: This merchant sells dyes of all colours and paintings, though buying and using the paintings is considered a Heresy. Be careful.
parts.translation: Этот торговец продает краски всех цветов и картин, хотя покупка и использование картин считается ересью. Будьте осторожны.

parts.body: This merchant sells foods and the infamous Malvasia wine, which magically increases the birthrate of Byzantine villages.
parts.translation: Этот торговец продает продукты и везде известное вино Мальвазия, которое волшебным образом увеличивает рождаемость византийских деревень.

parts.body: This merchant sells stone, sandstone and Byzantine tiles - All the materials aspiring Byzantine architects dream of.
parts.translation: Этот торговец продает камень, песчаник и византийскую плитку - все материалы, о которых мечтают византийские архитекторы.

parts.body: This merchant sells Icons of all sizes and invaluable frescos. Centurios pray for them to come.
parts.translation: Этот торговец продает иконы всех размеров и бесценные фрески. Веками молятся, ради того чтобы они пришли.

parts.body: This merchant sells carpets of all colours and Byzantine wool and silk clothes. Most male villagers fear for their savings.
parts.translation: Этот торговец продает ковры всех цветов и византийскую шерстяную и шелковую одежду. Большинство деревенских мужчин боятся за свои сбережения.

parts.body: Daily life and prayer are led by the Metropolitan in Religious villages.
parts.translation: Повседневной жизнью и молитвой руководит митрополит в религиозных деревнях.

parts.body: This Byzantine miner mines valuable blocks for his village.
parts.translation: Этот византийский шахтер добывает ценные блоки для своей деревни.

parts.body: The monks support the Metropolitan in his daily business and are painting beautiful frescos.
parts.translation: Монахи поддерживают митрополита в его повседневных делах и рисуют красивые фрески.

parts.body: The village pastor translates the will of God for the other villagers and makes sure children are guided to the faith, too.
parts.translation: Деревенский пастор переводит волю Божью для других жителей деревни.

parts.body: Like a normal soldier, but free to hire for the leader. And for everyone else, unfortunately.
parts.translation: Этот обученный византийский солдат будет сражаться за вас!

parts.body: The seamster weaves carpets from wool and Icons from silk, both of superior quality.
parts.translation: Портной плетет ковры из шерсти и иконы из шелка, оба высшего качества.

parts.body: The seamstress grows dandelions and creates clothes for the village.
parts.translation: Швея выращивает одуванчики и создает одежду для деревни.

parts.body: Every time that a sheep eats grass, the shepherd shears it. Or he slaughters it. Better stay away from him.
parts.translation: Каждый раз, когда овца ест траву, пастух стрижет ее.

parts.body: The silk farmer grows silkworms and is a master in Iconography.
parts.translation: Шелковист выращивает тутового шелкопряда и является мастером иконописи.

parts.body: The smelter mastered the highly complex mechanics of using furnaces. Other villagers shudder in awe.
parts.translation: Плавильня освоила сложнейшую механику использования печей. Другие жители содрогаются от страха.

parts.body: The soldier sometimes regrets choosing full training over marrying a beautiful woman.
parts.translation: Солдаты, подобные ему, сражаются, чтобы защитить Восточную Римскую империю!

parts.body: He forges the quality tools that make empires.
parts.translation: Он куёт качественные инструменты, которые создают империи.

parts.body: The wives do the household, cook the Byzantine meals, harvest grapes and share the latest gossip.
parts.translation: Жены занимаются домашним хозяйством, готовят византийские блюда, собирают виноград и делятся свежими сплетнями.

parts.body: The worker helps out the architect in building. Doing the same thing, he does not understand why the latter enjoys a higher status.
parts.translation: Рабочий помогает архитектору в строительстве. Делая то же самое, он не понимает, почему последний имеет более высокий статус.

parts.body: A village owned by a player who has earned the trust of the Byzantine people.
parts.translation: Византийская деревня игрока. Вся Римская империя верит в его лидерские качества.

parts.body: A village owned by a player who has earned the trust of the Byzantine people, but has asked for room for a little more creativity.
parts.translation: Византийская деревня игрока. Римская империя разочарована тем, что им не нравится их превосходная архитектура.

parts.body: Led by a Centurio in a massive fortress, the military village produces fine armoury, weaponry, olive oil and wine.
parts.translation: Военное поселение, которым управляет сотник в массивной крепости, производит прекрасное вооружение, оружие, оливковое масло и вино.

parts.body: Led by a Metropolitan, the religious village is known for their church, agricultural products and fine clothes from wool and silk.
parts.translation: Во главе с митрополитом, религиозное поселение известно своей церковью, сельскохозяйственной продукцией и прекрасной одеждой из шерсти и шелка.

parts.body: Led by a Baron, the trading village is built around a market sqaure and features fine wool and silk clothes and Malvasia wine.
parts.translation: Купеческое поселение, возглавляемое бароном, построено вокруг рыночной площади и украшено тонкой шерстяной и шелковой одеждой и вином Malvasia.

parts.body: In this well laid out grove Acacias are grown, serving as the prime fuel of the imperial furnaces.
parts.translation: В этой благоустроенной роще выращиваются акации, служащие основным топливом императорских печей.

parts.body: In this small grove Acacias are grown, despite the Byzantines not liking the colour of its wood.
parts.translation: В этой маленькой роще растут акации, несмотря на то, что византийцам не нравится цвет древесины.

parts.body: Just because this old place of worship seems to be plundered for building materials does not mean you should, too.
parts.job: ru|Just because this old place of worship seems to be plundered for building materials does not mean you should, too.

parts.body: This theatre seems to have had its last play aeons ago, but the clothes in its chest suggest otherwise.
parts.job: ru|This theatre seems to have had its last play aeons ago, but the clothes in its chest suggest otherwise.

parts.body: The house of the house builder who creates housing for the houseless. Of superior Byzantine quality, he added.
parts.translation: Студия архитектора, которая создает жилье для бездомных. Высшего византийского качества, добавил он.

parts.body: In the archives, all private information of the villagers are shown. If the villagers were literate, this building might spark a revolution.
parts.translation: В архивах показана вся личная информация жителей деревни. Если бы жители деревни были грамотными, это здание могло бы вызвать революцию.

parts.body: This lone Byzantine watchtower is a manifestation of the Roman claim to power.
parts.translation: Эта одинокая византийская сторожевая башня является проявлением притязаний римлян на власть.

parts.body: This field grows carrots. There is nothing more about it.
parts.translation: На этом поле растет морковь. В нём больше ничего нет.

parts.body: Not as big as a full church, but the local pastor assured that you get the same salvation when visiting a church service here.
parts.translation: Не такой большой, как полноценная церковь, но местный пастор заверил, что вы получите такое же спасение, посещая церковную службу здесь.

parts.body: A proud monument which is slowly growing to the sky and closer to God. It serves as the center of religious villages.
parts.translation: Гордый памятник, который медленно растет к небу и приближается к Богу. Он служит центром религиозных деревень.

parts.body: The chamber contains a bed and equipment to house a monk and keep him busy.
parts.job: ru|The chamber contains a bed and equipment to house a monk and keep him busy.

parts.body: This chamber contains a bed and equipment to house a yet another monk and keep him busy.
parts.job: ru|This chamber contains a bed and equipment to house a yet another monk and keep him busy.

parts.body: The sanctuary is the central piece of the church. The area behind the Iconostatis is reserved for the Clerics.
parts.job: ru|The sanctuary is the central piece of the church. The area behind the Iconostatis is reserved for the Clerics.

parts.body: The go-to destination if you are one of the cool kids of the village.
parts.job: ru|The go-to destination if you are one of the cool kids of the village.

parts.body: The warehouse stores valuable relics and books, and provides the Clerics with a place to paint frescos and Icons.
parts.job: ru|The warehouse stores valuable relics and books, and provides the Clerics with a place to paint frescos and Icons.

parts.body: Why settle for a small shrine?
This house features a loom to weave fine clothes, carpets and Icons. As purple is insufficient, dandelions are grown for yellow dye.
parts.translation: В этом доме есть ткацкий станок для плетения прекрасной одежды, ковров и икон.  Поскольку фиолетового недостаточно, одуванчики выращивают для желтого красителя.

parts.body: The farm is composed of a large house and a silo to be able to save wheat from mouses, which are yet to be seen in this world.
parts.translation: Ферма состоит из огромного дома и силоса, чтобы сохранить пшеницу от мышей, которых ещё никто не видел в этом мире.

parts.body: Fish, squid and snails appear magically in this pond. The Byzantines find use for all of them.
parts.translation: В этом пруду волшебным образом появляются рыба, кальмары и улитки.  Византийцы находят применение для всех них.

parts.body: The center of military villages. By personal request of the Centurio the architect tries to resemble the Theodisian walls.
parts.translation: Центр военных деревень.  По личной просьбе Центуриона архитектор старается воссоздать Феодосийские стены.

parts.body: The special layout of this forge allows the creation of maces and armour from the infamous Byzantine blue steel.
parts.job: ru|The special layout of this forge allows the creation of maces and armour from the infamous Byzantine blue steel.

parts.translation: В этой благоустроенной роще выращиваются ели, которые используются для интерьера византийских построек.

parts.body: In this small grove spruces are grown, as the Byzantines absolutely love the colour of its wood.
parts.translation: В этой небольшой роще растут ели, потому что византийцы обожают цвет этого дерева.

parts.body: This house is perfect to show that you have accumulated some wealth.
parts.translation: Этот дом — отличный способ показать, что вы накопили некоторое богатство.

parts.body: This massive plot comes with the guarantee that the local villagers won't tear down your buildings there.

parts.body: Buying this small hut is a good deal if you want to join the local village for some time.

parts.translation: Более бедные жены должны собирать песок, гравий и глину в этой яме, потому что песчаник невозможно найти вне пустыни.

parts.body: The most favourite animal of the Byzantines are pampered here.
parts.translation: Самое любимое животное византийцев живёт здесь.

parts.body: The silk farm is composed of sericultures, growing silkworms, to allow the Byzantines to create valuable Icons and clothes.

parts.body: Stuffed with furnaces, the smeltery serves as a resource hub for stone, glass and bricks.
parts.translation: Плавильная, заполненная печами, служит ресурсным центром для камня, стекла и кирпича.

parts.body: Probably the most visited building in a given village and the birthplace of delicate Malvasia wine.
parts.translation: Возможно, самое посещаемое здание в деревне и месторождение нежного вина Malvasia.

parts.translation: В этой кузнице создаются инструменты для обслуживания имперских нужд, ускорения различных задач.

parts.body: Manifested Late Roman Decadence. Don't even try to call it otherwise.
parts.translation: Проявленный позднеримский декаданс. Даже не пытайтесь назвать это иначе.

parts.body: Striding through the vineyards enhance the mood. Even when it is just the thought of a sweet bottle of Malvasia wine later that day.
parts.translation: Прогулки по виноградникам повышают настроение. Даже когда это просто мысль о сладкой бутылке вина Malvasia позднее в этот же день.

parts.body: Serving as the home of a village guard, the watchtower ensure protection for the whole village.
parts.translation: Служа домом деревенской стражи, сторожевая башня обеспечивает защиту всей деревни.

parts.body: <darkblue>Frequently Asked Questions
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Frequently Asked Questions

parts.body: <darkblue>The villagers speak in a language other than mine. Is this normal?
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>The villagers speak in a language other than mine. Is this normal?

parts.body: Millénaire villagers all speak in "their" language, such as Hindi for the Indians or French for the Normans. If you play in a different language, you will "learn" the language by interacting with them (trade, quests ...). As you “learn” their language, Millénaire will provide translations, first of the names of buildings, then of the types of villagers, and finally of the villager dialogues.
parts.job: ru|Millénaire villagers all speak in "their" language, such as Hindi for the Indians or French for the Normans. If you play in a different language, you will "learn" the language by interacting with them (trade, quests ...). As you “learn” their language, Millénaire will provide translations, first of the names of buildings, then of the types of villagers, and finally of the villager dialogues.

parts.body: Your most common exchanges with the villagers will be trading - you can sell many goods to them, and in return buy products, including blocks and objects specific to Millénaire. To trade with a village, go to the main building (or another store) and wait for a villager to come and see you with "Selling to the player" showing above his head. Then <darkblue>right-click<black>  him to open the trade screen.

parts.body: <darkblue>Reputation & village chief
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Reputation & village chief

parts.body: Each village in Millénaire has a opinion of you, neutral at the start and changing according to your actions. This reputation is very important: many rewards are only possible with a good reputation, and if your reputation gets too bad, villagers can refuse to trade with you. You can check your reputation by speaking (<darkblue>right-click<black>) with the village chief.

This reputation is very important: many rewards are only possible with a good reputation, and if your reputation gets too bad, villagers can refuse to trade with you. You can check your reputation by speaking (<darkblue>right-click<black>) with the village chief.

parts.body: The main way to improve your reputation is to trade with the village. Purchases as well as sales improve your reputation in proportion to the price. You can also improve your reputation by performing quests for them. Conversely, attacking a village or failling certain missions will damage your reputation.

parts.body: You also have a <darkblue>reputation with each culture<black>. This reputation is affected by all your dealings with villages of this culture, and affects your trading with all other villages of the same culture. For example, if you have a very good reputation with a Norman village, other Norman villages will also like you (a little) more. You can check your reputation with every culture in the information screen (“M” key by default).

parts.body: <darkblue>Village expansion
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Village expansion

parts.body: All villages start off small around a central building (of varying nature: fort, palace, monastery, etc ... commonly referred to as the "town hall"), with a few houses or other buildings. The villagers' main goal is to expand their village by selecting new buildings to build and improvements to existing buildings. For that reason, they need resources - they can produce some themselves (lumbermen harvest wood, and miners stone ...) but depend on the player for others. Their material needs for the planned construction are displayed in the main building. You can help by selling these resources first.

parts.body: The village population will also increase over time - at night, married villagers can have children. Once grown, these children move into new homes if available and become adults.

parts.body: The expansion of a village will cease in general two ways: either because the village has completed all buildable structures, or because it has no place. In the latter case, you can look at the village map to see which areas are unbuildable. It is sometimes possible to make them buildable, for example by filling in a lake.

parts.body: Sometimes, a village needs a block type that you can't craft yourself, such as Norman and Japanese timber frames. You must wait until the village builds a workshop and settles a child there as a craftsman.

parts.body: <darkblue>Combat and raiding
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Combat and raiding

parts.body: Millénaire is not always a peaceful mod: you can fight villagers, villages may conduct raids against each other, monsters can attack villages, and some isolated buildings are occupied by bandits. Whatever the circumstances, certain principles do not change: <darkblue>villagers are vulnerable only to direct attacks (melee, arrows and potions)<black>. They are not affected by fire, fall damage, or cactus. This restriction is intended to prevent the player from killing them without them being aware that the player is attacking them.

parts.body: Villagers vary in strength, and the equipment they wear can make them much more dangerous.

parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Respawning of villagers

parts.body: Once killed, a villager is temporarily dead. Dead villagers are respawned in their homes (but they will lose their equipment). After all, the player can respawn as well...

parts.body: <darkblue>Attack by players
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Attack by players

parts.body: You can always attack a villager, but other men of the village will then help to fight you. Should you manage to kill all the villagers of a village or lone building, the village's coffers will open and you can steal their contents.

parts.body: <darkblue>Bandits
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Bandits

parts.body: Some inhabitants of lone buildings will attack you without warning if you approach. Your reputation with their culture will not drop if you kill them. Like other villagers, they respawn at night - look under "<darkblue>destroy a village<black>" to see how to prevent it.

parts.body: <darkblue>Raids between villages
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Raids between villages

parts.body: Millénaire villages have positive or negative relations with nearby villages. These relations change randomly and may be influenced by the player talking to the chiefs of any of the villages. If their relations are very bad and one of the villages has enough fighters, it can launch a raid on other villages. You will be notified by a message. During a raid, the fighters attacking the town will be trying to kill the menfolk of the village they are attacking. If they do, they will take some of the resources as spoils. You can help one side or the other during a raid.

parts.body: It may be useful to encourage a village that you like to attack its neighbours to increase its resources. More cynically, encouraging raids can also allow you to help yourself to some of the loot once the defencers are dead.

parts.body: <darkblue>Spawning villages
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Spawning villages

parts.body: You can spawn a village type of your choice to the location of your choice with a Summoning Wand, an object that you can buy in any village whenever you have a sufficiently high reputation. To use the wand, put a gold block where you want to spawn a village and right-click the block with the wand. The subsequent screen allows you to choose the desired type of village.

parts.body: <darkblue>Destruction of a village or lone building
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Destruction of a village or lone building

parts.body: The inhabitants of a village or building respawn every night, even if you destroy all the buildings in the village. To prevent this (if you want to occupy the buildings yourself, for example), you must use the <darkblue>Wand of Negation<black>: you will find it in the chests of the main building once all the inhabitants are dead. Please note that the destruction of a village is irreversible.

parts.body: <darkblue>Player-controlled Villages
parts.job: ru|<darkblue>Player-controlled Villages

parts.body: It is possible to create a village with you as the leader, in which you can pick the locations of the buildings. To do this, you need to either be recognised as a leader in the culture of the village or to have completed the Creation Quest (see quests section), or to have increased your reputation to "natural leader" in a village and talk to its leader. You will then see an option to create player-controlled villages in the interface of the Summoning Wand.

parts.body: In player-controlled villages, you can order the construction of a new building using the wand at the desired location. An interface will open to allow you to choose the desired building. You can also allow or stop improvements to existing buildings via the "projects" panels. Trading resources with the villagers is unnecessary in these villages - just place items in the chests.

When a quest is available, it will be displayed above the head of a villager within square brackets, for example: "<darkblue>[Thirsty!]<black>." Right-click on it for a description of the task and the ability to accept or decline. Quests will be rewarded with money, reputation or objects. Some quests require you to have a good reputation with the village to be available.

parts.prefix: v2;60;Guy ka maas? Lekin ye toh dharm ke khilaaf hai! /
parts.body: Cow's meat? But eating it is against our dharma!
parts.translation: Коровье мясо? Но есть его против нашей религии!

parts.body: But what if it is tasty...?

parts.prefix: v2;180;Kya tum normandi ke jungli ho? /
parts.body: Are you a Norman barbarian?

rows.raw: //कभी सोचा है, गाय का मांस का क्या स्वाद हो सकता है?
//गाय का मांस? लेकिन यह धर्म के खिलाफ है!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Mai rasgulla chahta hoon. Mujhe bohot bhukh lagi hai! /
parts.body: I want a rasgulla. I am feeling very hungry!
parts.translation: Я хочу разгулу. Я очень голодна!

parts.prefix: v2;60;Nahi. Tumhe sirf chawal khaana chahiye. /
parts.body: No. You should eat only rice.
parts.translation: Нет. Ты должна есть только рис.

parts.prefix: v1;120;Lekin maine subhah hi ye khaya hai! /
parts.body: But I ate some this morning already!
And yesterday, and the day before...

parts.prefix: v2;220;Toh tum yahi aaj raat ko, kal, aur jeevan bhar khao! /
parts.body: And you will have to eat it tonight, tomorrow, and for the rest of your life!
parts.translation: И ты будешь есть это вечером, завтра и всю оставшуюся жизнь!

rows.raw: //मैं रसगुल्ला चाहता हु। मुझे भूख  लग रहा है ।

//तो तुम यही आज रात को, कल, और जीवन भर खाना!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Aaj maine bahut jyada lakdi kaat li! /
parts.body: I cut loads of wood today.

parts.prefix: v2;60;Tum hamare jungle ko reghistaan bana doge!        /
parts.body: You'll turn our forest into a desert!
parts.translation: Ты превратишь наш лес в пустыню!

parts.prefix: v1;120;Pareshan mat ho, yahaan bina kuch kiye hi pedh badhte hai. /
parts.body: Don't worry, here trees grow almost by themselves.
parts.translation: Не волнуйся, здесь деревья растут сами по себе.

rows.raw: //तुम हमारे गाँव को रेगिस्तान में बदल दोगे !

parts.prefix: v1;0;Mera mahal bahut chota ho gaya hai. /
parts.body: My palace has become very small.

parts.prefix: v2;60;Lekin maharaj, ye is kshetra me sabse bada hai! /
parts.body: But Maharaj, it is the biggest in the land!
parts.translation: Но Махарадж, он самый большой на территории!

parts.prefix: v1;120;Lekin ye mujhe chota lagne laga hai. /
parts.body: But to me it feels small.

rows.raw: //मेरा महल बहुत छोटा हो गया है |
//लेकिन महाराज, यह इस क्षेत्र में सबसे बड़ा है!
//लेकिन मुझे यह छोटा लगने लगा है |

parts.prefix: v1;0;Ek shaktishali qila hamare dushmanon ke khilaaf sabse accha bachaav hai. /
parts.body: A strong fort is the best defense against our enemies.
parts.translation: Сильная крепость - лучшая защита от наших врагов.

parts.body: What enemies, General?

parts.prefix: v1;100;Ye Norman aur anya jungli log. /
parts.body: The Normans and other barbarians.

rows.raw: //एक शक्तिशाली किले हमारे दुश्मनों के खिलाफ सबसे अच्छा बचाव है |

parts.prefix: v1;0;Mere pati amir aur prasidh hai. /
parts.body: My husband is rich and respectable.
Oh yes! It is true.

parts.prefix: v1;110;Par ve mere liye kabhi kuch laatey nahi hai. /

parts.translation: Тем не менее, он ничего мне не дарит.

parts.prefix: v2;160;Kyon nahi? Kal hi unhone tumhare liye teen sariyaan laayi thi. /
parts.body: Why not? Just yesterday he got you three saris.
parts.translation: Почему ничего? Только вчера он подарил тебе три сари.

rows.raw: //पर वे मेरे लिये कभी कुछ लाते नही है |

parts.prefix: v1;0;Aaj mere pati ne mere liye 50 tola sona kharida. /
parts.body: My husband bought fifty tolas of gold today.
parts.translation: Мой муж купил сегодня 50 тол золота.

parts.prefix: v2;60;50 tola sona! Mere paas sirf 10 tola sona hai... /
parts.body: Fifty tolas of gold! I have just 10 tolas...
parts.translation: 50 тол золота! У меня только 10 тол...

parts.prefix: v1;120;Aasha hai ki sitaare tumhare paksh mein honge. /
parts.body: Let’s hope that the stars line up in your favour.
parts.translation: Будем надеяться, что звёзды выстроятся в Вашу милость.

rows.raw: //आज मेरे पति ने मेरे लिये 50 तोला सोना खरीदा |

//आशा है कि सितारों तुम्हारे पक्ष में होंगे|

parts.prefix: v1;0;Mujhe pratimaon banane ka achha mauka mila hai. /
parts.body: I have got a great opportunity to make statues.
parts.translation: У меня есть отличная возможность сделать статуи.

parts.prefix: v2;50;Tum bahut achhe murtiyan banate ho.        /
parts.body: That's because you make very good statues.
parts.translation: Это потому что вы делаете очень хорошие статуи.

parts.prefix: v1;100;Main pandhara saal se murtiyan bana raha hoon. /
parts.body: I've been making statues for quite some time.
parts.translation: Я уже делаю статуи довольно давно.

rows.raw: //मुझे प्रतिमाओं बनाने का अच्छा मौका मिला है|

parts.prefix: v1;0;Hame aur phavadon ki zarurat hai. /
parts.body: We need more pickaxes.
I am busy right now.

parts.prefix: v2;150;Uff! Mujhe kitna kaam karna padta hai! /
parts.body: Uff! I have to do so much work!
parts.translation: Уфф! Я должен сделать так много работы!

rows.raw: //उफ़फ़! मुझे कितना काम करना पडता है !

parts.prefix: v1;0;<targetname>, shayad gaon ke nikat daaku hai! /
parts.body: <targetname>, I think there are bandits lurking near our village!
parts.translation: <targetname>, Я думаю, что есть бандиты, скрывающиеся возле нашей деревни!

parts.prefix: v2;50;Chinta mat karo, main gaon ki raksha karonga. /
parts.body: Don't worry, I will protect the village.
You are so strong!
And handsome, too.

parts.prefix: v1;150;Agar aap ke paas moonch na hoti... /
parts.body: If it weren't for your moustache...

parts.prefix: v2;200;Meri moonch ke baare main kuch bhi na kaho! /
parts.body: Not a word about my moustache!

rows.raw: //<targetname>, शायद गांव के निकट डाकू है!

parts.body: My lord, the harvest is not good this year.
parts.translation: Милорд, урожай в этом году не очень хороший.

parts.prefix: v2;40;Tu aalsi hai! Jyada kaam kar! /
parts.body: That's because you are lazy! Do more work!
parts.translation: Это потому что ты ленивый! Делай больше работы!

parts.body: But it hasn't rained at all...

parts.prefix: v2;120;Meri galti nahi hai. Mujhe apna paisa chahiye. /
parts.body: It's not my fault. I want my rent money.
parts.translation: Это не моя вина. Я хочу свою арендную плату.

parts.prefix: v1;170;Lekin mere paas paise nahi hai. /
parts.body: But I have no money.
Then give me back the land.

parts.prefix: v1;260;Mere paas kuch bhi nahi rehe jayega! /
parts.body: But I will have nothing left!
parts.translation: Тогда у меня ничего не останется!

rows.raw: //सेनापति, इस साल फसल अच्छी नहीं है |

//मेरी पास कुछ भी नही रह जाएगा!

parts.prefix: v1;0;Vaha Vyapaari apne ghar ke bagal mein ek naya ghar ban rahe hai. /
parts.body: That trader is building a new house next to his own.
parts.translation: Этот торговец строит новый дом рядом со своим.

parts.body: Another house? But why does he need a new one?
parts.translation: Ещё один дом? Но зачем ему нужен новый?

parts.prefix: v1;90;Vaha naya ghar unke betey ke liye hai. /
parts.body: The new house is for his son.

parts.prefix: v1;140;Jab unke betey ki shaadi hogi, tab dono paas me honge. /
parts.body: When his son will get married, both father and son will be next to each other.
parts.translation: Когда его сын женится, они будут рядом.

rows.raw: //वह व्यापारी अपने घर के बगल में एक नया घर बना रहे है|
//वह नया घर अपने बेटे के लिए है |
//जब उनके बेटे की शादी होगी, तब दोनों पास में होंगे |

parts.prefix: v1;0;Gaon ke mukhiye ne apni patni ke liye sone ke kangan laaye. /
parts.body: The village chief got his wife gold bracelets.
parts.translation: Деревенский вождь подарил своей жене золотые браслеты.

parts.prefix: v1;60;Par aap mere liye kuch nahi laatey... /
parts.body: But you've never gotten any jewellery for me...
parts.translation: Но у тебя никогда не было украшений для меня...

parts.prefix: v2;110;Tumhe ek amir aadmi se shaadi karni chahiye thi. /
parts.body: You should have married a rich man.
parts.translation: Ты должна выйти замуж за богатого мужчину.

parts.prefix: v1;160;Lekin mujhe aur dahej dena padta. /
parts.body: But then I would have had to pay more dowry.
parts.translation: Но тогда мне пришлось бы платить больше приданого.

parts.prefix: v2;200;Fir tumhe bhagyawaan lagna chahiye ki main tumhara pati hoon. /
parts.body: Then you should feel blessed to have a husband like me.
parts.translation: Тогда ты должна быть счастлива, имея такого мужа, как я.

rows.raw: //गांव के मुखिये ने अपनी पत्नी के लिये सोने के कंगन लाये|

//तुम्हे एक अमीर आदमी से शादी करनी चाहए थी |
//फिर तुम्हे भाग्यावान लगना चाहिए की मैं तुम्हारा पति हूं|

parts.prefix: v1;0;Maine bahit dinon se sharaab nahi piya hai. /
parts.body: I haven't had alcohol for a long time.
parts.translation: У меня уже давно не было алкоголя.

parts.prefix: v2;50;Gaon ke bahar ek aadmi sharaab aur moongfali bechta hai. /
parts.body: There is a man who sits under the banyan tree outside the village and sells alcohol and peanuts.
parts.translation: Есть человек, который сидит под деревом баньян за деревней и продает алкоголь и арахис.

parts.prefix: v1;110;Sach? Maine socha tha ki gaon mein sharaab par pratibandh laga diya gaya hai. /
parts.body: Really? I thought it was forbidden to sell alcohol in the village!
parts.translation: В самом деле? Я думал, что продавать алкоголь в деревне запрещено!

parts.prefix: v2;160;Yeh kisi aur ko mat batana. /
parts.body: Don't tell anyone else.

parts.prefix: v1;200;Chalo, hum aaj shaam ko vahan jaatey hai. /
parts.body: Ok, let’s go there today in the evening.
parts.translation: Хорошо, давай сходим к нему сегодня вечером.

rows.raw: //मैने कई दिनों से शराब नही पिया है|

parts.body: Did you get me some toys?

rows.raw: //क्या आप ने मेरे लिये खिलौने लेय?

parts.prefix: v1;0;Mere paas bahut saare dost hai.         /
parts.body: I have many friends.

parts.prefix: v1;0;Meri maa shaam ko mujhe khelne nahi deti hai. /
parts.body: My mother doesn't allow me to play after dark.
parts.translation: Моя мама не разрешает мне играть после наступления темноты.

Did you see that?
See what?

rows.raw: //* The part before the ";" is the title, after it the description

parts.body: Stranger
We are not used to foreigners in our remote village.
parts.translation: Мы не привыкли к чужим в нашем поселении.

parts.body: Familiarity
So far, you have not committed any major breach of custom.
parts.translation: Пока ты не совершил каких-либо серьезных нарушений обычаев.

parts.body: Known Face
You seem to have made a good impression on many of us. Continue, and we will both benefit.
parts.translation: Похоже, ты произвел хорошее впечатление на многих из нас. Продолжай, и мы оба выиграем.

parts.body: Regular Visitor
Namaste, $name-ji! What news do you bring?
Fellow Neighbor
While you are not perfect, we acknowledge that you have been a good neighbor $name-ji. We enjoy your company.
parts.translation: Хотя вы не совершенны, мы признаем, что вы были хорошим соседом $name-жи. Нам нравится ваша компания.

parts.body: Favourite Trader
Welcome back, $name. What have you brought to trade with us?
parts.translation: С возвращением, $name. Что за товары у тебя для нас?

parts.body: Friend of the Village
$name-ji, we all consider you a true friend here.
parts.translation: $name-жи, мы все считаем тебя истинным другом.

parts.body: A True Ally
You are a true ally of this village $name-ji! If you ever need refuge, you can stay in our village.
parts.translation: Вы настоящий союзник этой деревни $name-жи! Если вам когда-нибудь понадобится убежище, вы можете остаться в нашей деревне.

parts.body: One of Us
I would not thought I would live to see a foreign accepted in the village, but $name-ji, you are one of us now!
parts.translation: Я не думал, что доживу до того, что кто-либо из чужеземцев будет общепринят в нашем поселении, но $name-жи, теперь ты один из нас!

parts.body: Natural Leader
$name-ji, you have gained the trust and respect of my people. They will follow you anywhere.
parts.translation: $name-жи, ты заслужил доверие и уважение моих людей. Они последуют за тобой всюду.

parts.body: Overachieving Rajput

The Indian people are extremely happy that you've wanted to stay with them and help them with their struggles! In case you haven't noticed, we've created 5 other amazing cultures that will probably give you a better reward than a lackluster and disappointing message.
parts.translation: Индийский народ очень рад, что вы захотели остаться с ним и помочь им в их борьбе! В случае, если вы не заметили, мы создали 5 других удивительных культур, которые, вероятно, дадут вам лучшую награду, чем это тусклое и разочаровывающее сообщение.

parts.body: Nuisance
We do not like foreigners here, especially of your kind.
parts.translation: Мы не любим чужих здесь, особенно таких как ты.

parts.body: Unpleasant Outsider
Whoever raised you did a very poor job. We hope you will be gone soon.
parts.translation: Как мы поняли, твои поступки очень плохи. Мы надеемся, что ты уйдешь отсюда как можно скорее.

parts.body: Public Enemy
Every morning I pray the Goddess I will never see your face again.
parts.translation: Каждое утро я молюсь Богине, чтобы больше никогда не видеть твоей мерзкой рожи.

parts.body: I’ve had enough vegetarian curry!

parts.prefix: indian_peasantwife.DeliverGoodsHousehold=Uffh, itna sara khana akeley kaisey leh jaoongi. /
parts.body: How will I carry all this food alone?
parts.job: ru|How will I carry all this food alone?

parts.prefix: indian_peasantwife.GetGoodsHousehold=Inkey liye chahey jitna bhi khana lao, kam padta hai. /
parts.body: No matter how much you get for this family, it is never enough!
parts.job: ru|No matter how much you get for this family, it is never enough!

parts.prefix: indian_peasantwife.GetHouseTHResources=Sab kuch toh thakur ko dey dena padta hai. /
parts.body: Everything always ends up in the landlord’s house.
parts.job: ru|Everything always ends up in the landlord’s house.

parts.body: The kids love rasgullas.
parts.job: ru|The kids love rasgullas.

parts.prefix: indian_sculptor.Scult=Murtikala ched aur gaanth ki kala hai. /
parts.body: Sculpture is the art of the hole and the lump.
parts.job: ru|Sculpture is the art of the hole and the lump.

parts.prefix: indian_smith.MakeTools=Sabhi merey banaye huye upkaran istamal kartey hain, phir bhi mujhey neecha samachtey hain. /
parts.body: Everyone uses my tools, and yet everyone looks down on me.
parts.job: ru|Everyone uses my tools, and yet everyone looks down on me.

parts.prefix: male.BecomeAdult=Main badey hokar yodhdha ban-na chahta tha. /
parts.body: I wanted to become a great warrior when I was younger...
parts.job: ru|I wanted to become a great warrior when I was younger...

parts.body: I will go to rest now.
I am tired.

parts.prefix: male.gorest=Subah sey kaam kar raha hoon. /
parts.body: I have been working since the morning.

parts.body: Everything is grown by my family, deep in the jungle.
parts.job: ru|Everything is grown by my family, deep in the jungle.

parts.prefix: merchant_adivasi.greeting=Main van se a raha hoon /
parts.body: I have just come from the forest.
See the riches of Persia!
parts.job: ru|See the riches of Persia!

parts.body: Peace upon you, brother!

parts.prefix: merchant_villagewoman.KeepStall=Ghara ka bana khana, bhukhe yaatriyon ke lie! /
parts.body: Home-made food for hungry travelers!
parts.job: ru|Home-made food for hungry travelers!

parts.prefix: merchant_villagewoman.greeting=Ek akeelii mahila ke lie safar karna mushkil hai /
parts.body: Traveling is tough for a lone woman.
parts.translation: Путешествия очень тяжелы для одинокой женщины.

parts.prefix: villager.BecomeAdult=Khel kud bahut ho gaya, ab kaam par chalo. /
parts.body: Enough playing, time to work.
parts.job: ru|Enough playing, time to work.

parts.prefix: villager.GoPlay=Mujjhey mitti sey khelna accha lagta hai. /
parts.body: I love playing in the dirt.
parts.job: ru|I love playing in the dirt.

parts.prefix: villager.childobserveagriculture=Phasalon ko ropan karana har din bahut ubaoo lagata hai. Mujhe saahas ka jeevan chaahie! /
parts.body: Planting crops all days seems so boring. I want a life of adventure!
parts.translation: Высаживать семена днями напролёт так скучно. Я хочу жизнь, полную приключений!

parts.prefix: villager.childobserveconstruction=Nirmaan mere lie bahut adhik kaam kee tarah dikhata hai. /
parts.body: Construction looks like too much work for me.
parts.translation: Строительство выглядит слишком тяжелым для меня.

parts.body: Such strong arms!

parts.prefix: villager.childobserveproducefood=Meri Ma sabase achchhe rasagulle banaati hai. /

parts.prefix: villager.childeatsugarcane=Ma kahati hain ki yah daanton ko nukasaan pahunchaata hai, lekin yah bahut achchha hai! /
parts.body: Mum says it damages the teeth, but it's so good!
parts.translation: Мама говорит, что это повреждает зубы, но оно такое вкусное!

parts.prefix: villager.HarvestRice=Adbhut baarish ke mausam kee vajah se, ab hamaare paas ek majaboot phasal hai.. /

parts.job: ru|Because of the wonderful raining season, we now have a strong harvest.

parts.prefix: villager.HarvestTurmeric=Haldi ki kheti kartey kartey merey haath peeley ho gayein hain. /

parts.job: ru|This turmeric harvesting is making my hands yellow.

parts.prefix: villager.PlantRice=Is saal barish achchi hui toh phasal accha hoga. /

parts.job: ru|If it rains heavily, the harvest will be good this year.

parts.body: After all, everyone needs turmeric.
parts.job: ru|After all, everyone needs turmeric.

parts.body: Defeat to the enemies!
Victory will be ours.

parts.prefix: villager.calltoarms=Sab apney apney hathiyar utha lo! /

parts.prefix: villager.gopray=Bhagwan, bas aap hi ka sahara hai. /

parts.translation: Господи, пусть этот сезон принесет хороший урожай.

parts.prefix: villager.gopray=Hey Bhagwan, is baar phasal achhi ho. /

It is very hot today.

How are things?

parts.body: Are you from beyond the ocean?
Greetings, $name-ji!
parts.job: ru|Greetings, $name-ji!

parts.prefix: villager.greeting=Yeh barish kyun nahin ho rahiee hai? /
parts.body: Why isn’t it raining here?

parts.prefix: villager.inspectconstruction=Mujhe lagata hai ki hamaare raajamistree aise achchhe kaam karate hain. /
parts.body: I enjoy seeing our builders produce such fine works.
parts.translation: Мне нравится, когда наши строители проводят такие прекрасные работы.
